The animals knew they had to do something about the garbage. They all worked together to clean it up. They picked up the garbage and put it in a big bag. They were happy to have helped make the forest clean again.

Suddenly, a kind fisherman came and saw Timmy in the net. The fisherman knew what to do and helped Timmy get free. Sammy was so happy and felt safe again. He learned that sometimes it's okay to surrender and ask for help when you need it.

From that day on, Sammy made sure to always be careful and watch out for his friends in the ocean. He knew that being safe was the most important thing.

Max asked, "What does 'spoiled' mean?" His friend said, "It means it's not good to eat anymore." Max said, "Oh, I guess I won't try it then." Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Tim went first and slid down fast. He laughed and said, "That was fun! Come on, Sam, try it!"

Sam looked at the slide and felt fearful. It was too high and too steep for him. He said, "No, thank you, Tim. I don't want to slide. I want to play with the green ball."

Tim rolled his eyes and said, "Don't be a baby, Sam. Sliding is easy and fun. You just have to close your eyes and go. Don't you want to be brave like me?"

Sam shook his head and said, "No, thank you, Tim. I don't want to be brave like you. I want to be happy like me. I like the green ball. It is soft and round and bouncy. It makes me smile."

Tim sighed and said, "Fine, Sam. You can play with the green ball. But you are missing out on the slide. It is the best thing in the park."

Tim went back to the slide and slid down again and again. He did not notice that the sky was getting dark and the wind was getting strong. He did not hear his mom calling him to go home. He only cared about the slide.

Sam played with the green ball and saw the clouds and heard the wind. He heard his mom calling him to go home. He picked up the green ball and ran to his mom. He said, "Mom, let's go home. It is going to rain soon."

Mom smiled and said, "Good job, Sam. You are very smart and careful. You know how to watch the weather and listen to me. Where is Tim?"

Sam pointed to the slide and said, "Tim is still sliding. He does not want to stop. He says he is brave."

Mom frowned and said, "Tim is not brave. He is foolish. He does not know how to watch the weather and listen to me. He is in danger of getting wet and cold and sick. Come on, Sam, let's go get him."

Mom and Sam went to the slide and found Tim. He was wet and cold and shivering. He was not laughing anymore. He was crying and saying, "Mom, I'm sorry. I was wrong. I should have listened to you and Sam. I should have stopped sliding and gone home. I was not brave. I was stupid."

Mom hugged Tim and said, "It's okay, Tim. I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you can learn from it. Next time, you will be more smart and careful. You will watch the weather and listen to me. You will know when to have fun and when to go home. You will be brave in the right way."

Mom took Tim and Sam home. She gave them warm clothes and hot soup. She kissed them and said, "I love you both. You are my good boys. You can play in the park again tomorrow. But remember, the slide is not the only thing that is fun. The green ball is fun too. And so is being happy and safe and healthy."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of being smart and careful, listening to parents, and knowing when to have fun and when to stop. It also shows that being brave does not mean being reckless or stubborn, but being wise and responsible. It also shows that different things can make different people happy, and that happiness is more important than pride.

Lily was not afraid of the alligator. She thought he was cute and wanted to pet him. She opened the door of the boat and stepped out. "Don't worry, Max, I'll make friends with him. Maybe he's lonely and just wants to play."

Max tried to stop her. He grabbed her arm and pulled her back. "No, Lily, don't go! He might bite you or drag you under the water. He's dangerous. Stay in the boat with me."

But Lily did not listen. She insisted on going to the alligator. She said, "He won't hurt me, Max. He's nice. Look, he's smiling at me. Maybe he's a wealthy alligator who lives in a big castle under the water. Maybe he'll invite us to his home and give us lots of toys and candy."

She let go of Max's arm and walked towards the alligator. She reached out her hand to touch his nose. But before she could, the alligator snapped his jaws and lunged at her. Lily screamed and ran back to the boat. Max slammed the door and locked it. They hugged each other and cried.

The alligator banged on the box and tried to get in. He was angry and hungry. He wanted to eat the twins. But he could not break the box. It was too strong and hard. He gave up and swam away.

Lily and Max learned their lesson. They never played with the alligator again. They stayed in their boat and sailed to a safer island. They were happy and safe.

Max was a good friend and did not give up. He showed Sam again and again. Finally, Sam understood how to stand and catch the ball. They played together all day and became the best of friends. And from that day on, Max and Sam always played together, and they both understood what it meant to be a good friend.

He looked for his guitar under the tree, but it was gone. Tim had to go home without his guitar. He could not play music for his friends. Tim lied on his bed and cried. He missed his guitar very much.

Lily's grandpa felt bad for forgetting the newspaper the first day and for bringing a wet one the next day. He promised to never forget again and to make sure the newspaper was always dry. From that day on, Lily and her grandpa enjoyed reading the newspaper together every morning.

Lily's grandpa told her that it's important to release the fish back into the water after catching it, so it can swim freely and grow bigger. Lily was sad to let go of the fish, but she knew it was the right thing to do. 

From that day on, Lily always made sure to release the fish she caught back into the water. She learned that it's important to take care of the animals and the environment around us.

Once upon a time, there was a bus driver named Bob. He loved his job and he loved driving his bus. One day, he saw a rare flower on the side of the road. He stopped the bus and got out to take a closer look. It was so pretty!

Bob wanted to show the flower to his passengers, so he picked it up and brought it onto the bus. But, he didn't realize that the flower had bugs on it. When he got back on the bus, the bugs started to spray everywhere! The passengers were scared and didn't know what to do.

Bob quickly realized his mistake and apologized to his passengers. He learned that sometimes, it's better to leave rare things where they are and not bring them onto the bus. The moral of the story is to always be careful and think before you act.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals who were always fighting. The lion would roar at the monkey, and the monkey would throw a banana at the lion. The elephant would stomp his feet, and the giraffe would stick out his long neck. They could never agree on anything.

One day, a wise old owl came to visit the animals. "Why do you fight?" he asked. "We don't like each other," said the lion. "We don't trust each other," said the monkey. "We don't need each other," said the elephant. "But you do," said the owl. "You all have something to offer. If you unite, you can accomplish great things together."

The animals thought about what the owl said. They realized that they could depend on each other. The lion could protect them, the monkey could climb trees to get food, the elephant could carry heavy things, and the giraffe could reach high places. They decided to stitch together a plan to work together.

From that day on, the animals lived in peace and harmony. They learned that they could accomplish anything if they worked together and were dependable on each other. The moral of the story is that it's better to work together than to fight with each other.

Sam and Lily were brother and sister. They liked to play at the beach. They liked to build sand castles and look for shells. But sometimes they fought over the toys and the space.

One day, they went to the beach with their mom and dad. They saw an enormous sand castle near the water. It had towers and walls and flags. Sam and Lily wanted to play with it. They ran to the sand castle and each grabbed a toy. Sam took a shovel and Lily took a bucket.

"Hey, that's mine!" Sam shouted.

"No, it's mine!" Lily shouted back.

They pulled and tugged at the toys. They made the sand castle fall down. They made a big mess. They made the other kids who built the sand castle cry.

Their mom and dad came over. They were not happy. They scolded Sam and Lily for being rude and selfish. They told them to say sorry and to share the toys. They told them to help rebuild the sand castle.

Sam and Lily felt bad. They said sorry to the other kids. They gave back the toys. They asked if they could help. The other kids nodded. They smiled. They gave Sam and Lily some tools and some tips.

Together, they worked on the sand castle. They used the shovel and the bucket and the molds and the sticks. They made new towers and walls and flags. They made the sand castle bigger and better than before. They had fun. They made friends.

Sam and Lily learned a lesson. They learned to unite and not to fight. They learned to be kind and not to mind. They learned to enjoy the beach and not to breach. They hugged each other and their mom and dad. They thanked the other kids for letting them play. They had a great day at the beach.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to draw. They had many crayons of different colors, but they always wanted more. One day, they saw a big box of crayons at the store. It had 100 crayons, some with glitter and some with stripes. Tom and Lily wanted to buy the box, but it was very expensive.

They asked their mom to buy it for them, but she said no. She said they had enough crayons at home, and they should save their money for something else. Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They decided to take the box of crayons when their mom was not looking. They put it in their backpack and ran out of the store.

When they got home, they opened the box and started to draw. They used the glitter and striped crayons to make wild pictures of animals and monsters. They had fun, but they also felt guilty. They knew they had done something bad. They had stolen the crayons from the store.

The next day, their mom found the box of crayons in their room. She was very upset. She asked them where they got it. Tom and Lily could not lie. They told her the truth. They said they were sorry and they wanted to return the crayons to the store.

Their mom was disappointed, but she was also proud that they admitted their mistake. She took them to the store and made them apologize to the owner. The owner was angry, but he also forgave them. He said they could keep one crayon each, but they had to pay for the rest. Tom and Lily chose their favorite crayons and gave the rest back. They also gave some of their money to the owner.

Tom and Lily learned a lesson that day. They learned that stealing is wrong and that they should be happy with what they have. They also learned that honesty is important and that saying sorry can make things better. They drew a picture for their mom with their new crayons. They wrote "We love you" on it. Their mom smiled and hugged them. She said she loved them too.

Here is one possible story, but there are many other ways to write it.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play on the farm. They had a new goat named Spot who was very soft and friendly. They liked to feed him grass and pet him and hug him. But Spot did not like to share his food or his space. He would complain and bleat and push the other animals away.

One day, Anna and Ben decided to take Spot for a walk in the woods. They put a rope around his neck and led him along the path. They saw many things in the woods, like birds and flowers and bugs. They wanted to show Spot how nice the woods were, but Spot did not care. He only wanted to eat and be alone.

Soon, they came to a bridge over a stream. The bridge was old and weak and had holes in it. Anna and Ben did not know that, but Spot did. He smelled something bad under the bridge. He heard a growl and a snort. He knew there was a big bad wolf hiding there, waiting for someone to cross. Spot was scared, but he did not tell Anna and Ben. He wanted to get rid of them, so he could run away.

He pulled on the rope and made Anna and Ben follow him. He ran across the bridge as fast as he could. He did not care if the bridge broke or if Anna and Ben fell. He only wanted to save himself. But he was too late. The wolf jumped out of his hiding place and bit Spot's leg. Spot screamed and kicked and tried to get free, but the wolf was stronger and hungrier. He dragged Spot under the bridge and ate him up.

Anna and Ben heard Spot's scream and saw the wolf. They were very scared and sad. They dropped the rope and ran back to the farm. They told their mom and dad what happened. They cried and cried and wished they had been nicer to Spot. They learned that being selfish and mean can have a bad ending.

Sara and Ben like to play with their old map. It is a big paper with many colors and shapes. They pretend it is a treasure map and they look for clues.

One day, they find a big X on the map. They think it is where the treasure is. They want to go there and see what it is.

"Let's test our map and find the treasure!" Sara says.

"OK, but how do we know where to go?" Ben asks.

"We have to follow the map. See, it has arrows and numbers. They tell us how to walk and how far to go." Sara explains.

They take the map and start to walk. They count their steps and turn when the map says so. They have fun and see many things on the way. They see a bird, a flower, a rock and a cloud.

After a while, they reach the big X. They are very excited. They look around and see a big tree. Under the tree, there is a box. It is old and dusty.

"Wow, maybe this is the treasure!" Ben says.

"Let's open it and see!" Sara says.

They open the box and find many things inside. They find a book, a hat, a ball and a toy car. They are very happy. They think the map is magic and it gave them a gift.

"Thank you, map!" they say.

They hug the map and the box. They decide to share the things and play with them. They think they are the best explorers ever. They smile and laugh.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and find things. Sometimes they found shells, or rocks, or coins. But today they found something very different.

"Look, look!" Sara shouted. "I found a skeleton!"

Ben ran over to see. He saw a big pile of bones in the sand. They were white and hard and had holes in them. They looked like a puzzle.

"Wow, that's cool!" Ben said. "Can I see?"

Sara nodded and handed him a bone. It was long and thin and had a pointy end. Ben pretended it was a sword and waved it around.

"Ha, ha, I'm a pirate!" he said.

Sara laughed and picked up another bone. It was round and had lots of teeth. She pretended it was a monster and made scary noises.

"Roar, roar, I'm a dinosaur!" she said.

They had fun playing with the skeleton. They made up stories and jokes and sounds. They forgot about everything else.

But then they heard a voice.

"Hey, what are you doing with my skeleton?" the voice said.

They looked up and saw a man. He was wearing a hat and a coat and had a big bag. He looked angry.

"That's my skeleton!" he said again. "I dug it up from the ground. It's very old and very rare. It's mine!"

Sara and Ben felt scared. They didn't know the man. They didn't know he had a skeleton. They thought they had found it.

"Sorry, mister," Sara said. "We didn't know. We were just playing."

"Yeah, sorry," Ben said. "We didn't mean to take it."

They gave the bones back to the man. He put them in his bag and walked away. He didn't say thank you. He didn't say goodbye.

Sara and Ben felt sad. They liked the skeleton. They wanted to play with it more. But they knew they had to share. They knew they couldn't keep it.

They looked at each other and smiled.

"That was fun, though," Sara said.

"Yeah, it was," Ben said.

They hugged and went back to digging. They hoped they would find something new. Something they could keep. Something they could share.

They take a small bucket and a shovel and go to the garden. They dig in different places and find different kinds of soil. Some soil is brown, some is black, some is red and some is yellow. They put some of each kind in their bucket.

"Look, Tom, this soil is very soft and smooth," Sara says, touching the black soil.

"And this soil is very hard and rough," Tom says, tapping the red soil.

They compare the different soils and talk about how they feel and look. They think soil is very interesting and beautiful.

They fill their bucket with soil and go back to their box. They make a space for their new collection. They pour the soil in the box and make a rainbow with the different colors.

"Wow, Sara, our soil collection is the most beautiful one," Tom says, admiring their work.

"I agree, Tom, soil is amazing," Sara says, smiling.

They are very happy with their collection. They decide to collect more things tomorrow. They wonder what they will find.

"Help! Help! Help!" They shout.

Mom and Dad hear them and run to their room. They open the door and see the fire and the smoke and the mess. They see Luna and Tom and Mia. They are angry and worried.

"Stop! Stop! Stop!" Mom and Dad yell. They grab a blanket and wrap it around Luna. They put out the fire and the matches. They check if Luna and Tom and Mia are okay. They are not hurt, but they are very sorry.

They watch a movie and eat popcorn. They are happy and safe. They learned their lesson. They never play with matches again.

One day, they had a problem. They both wanted the same train. It was a red train with a shiny whistle. It was also very fragile. It could break easily if they pulled or pushed it too hard. They started to argue and tug on the train.

"No, mine!" said Ben.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the red train and the track. She saw Anna and Ben looking angry and sad.

"Stop, stop!" she said. "You need to discuss. Discuss means to talk and listen. You can take turns with the train or find another way to play. But you can't fight over it. It is fragile and it is not nice."

Anna and Ben looked at their mom. They knew she was right. They did not want to break the train or hurt each other. They decided to discuss. They said sorry and gave each other a hug. Tom and Lily liked to play in the river. They had a big raft that they could sit on and paddle with sticks. They pretended they were pirates and explorers, looking for treasure and islands.

One day, they saw a big fish in the water. It was shiny and had a long tail. Tom wanted to catch the fish and put it in a bucket. He said, "Look, Lily, a fish! Let's get it!"

Lily was scared of the fish. She thought it might bite them or flip the raft. She said, "No, Tom, leave the fish alone. It is not our fish. It is a wild fish. It wants to swim and be free."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He leaned over the raft and tried to grab the fish with his hands. The fish was fast and slippery. It splashed Tom with water and made him lose his balance. Tom fell off the raft and into the river.

Lily screamed and reached for Tom. She was worried he might drown or get hurt by the fish. She said, "Tom, Tom, are you okay? Come back to the raft!"

Tom was not okay. He was wet and cold and scared. He did not like the fish anymore. He wanted to quit playing and go home. He said, "Lily, help me! I don't like the river. I don't like the fish. I want to quit!"

Lily pulled Tom back to the raft. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm here. You're safe. Let's quit playing and go home. We can have some soup and warm up. Maybe we can play something else later. Something that is more fun and less scary."

Tom nodded and said, "Okay, Lily. Thank you. You're a good sister. I'm sorry I was silly. Let's go home."

They paddled the raft back to the shore. They left the fish alone. They went home and had some soup. They felt better and warmer. They decided to play with their blocks and dolls instead. They were happy and healthy. They learned to be careful and kind. They loved each other. The end.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to play outside at night. They would look at the stars and the moon and make up stories about them. One night, they saw a big bright moon that was full and round. They decided to play a game of twist.

"Let's see who can twist the most without falling down," Tom said. "I bet I can twist more than you."

"No, I can twist more than you," Mia said. "You always fall down first."

They started to twist their bodies around and around, laughing and counting. Tom twisted faster and faster, trying to beat Mia. Mia twisted slower and slower, feeling dizzy.

"Tom, stop, I feel sick," Mia said. "I can't twist anymore."

But Tom did not hear her. He was too busy twisting and trying to win. He twisted so much that he did not see the big rock behind him. He twisted right into the rock and hit his head. He fell down with a thud and a cry.

Mia stopped twisting and ran to Tom. She saw blood on his head and tears in his eyes. She felt sorry and scared. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to make you twist so much. Are you okay?"

Tom felt a harsh pain in his head and a harsh anger in his heart. He pushed Mia away and said, "Go away, Mia. You made me twist too much. You made me hurt myself. I don't want to play with you anymore."

Mia felt a harsh sadness in her chest and a harsh coldness in the air. She looked at the moon and wished it would make Tom feel better. She wished they could be friends again. She wished they could play twist again. But the moon did not answer. It just shone brightly and silently, like a big round eye.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a big box of colorful balls in the basement. They decided to have fun with them and fill the bathroom with them. They carried the balls upstairs and threw them into the bathtub, the sink, the toilet and the floor. They laughed and giggled as they made a mess.

Mom was in the kitchen, making lunch. She did not hear the noise from the bathroom. She thought Lily and Max were playing peacefully in their room. She was happy and relaxed.

Soon, the bathroom was full of balls. Lily and Max could not fit any more. They looked at their work and felt proud. They wanted to show Mom what they had done. They ran to the kitchen and shouted, "Mom, Mom, come and see! We filled the bathroom with balls!"

Mom followed them, curious and smiling. But when she saw the bathroom, she gasped and frowned. She was angry and shocked. She said, "Lily and Max, what have you done? You made a huge mess! You wasted water and soap! You could have broken something or hurt yourself! This is not a game, this is a disaster!"

Lily and Max felt sorry and scared. They realized they had done something bad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We just wanted to have fun. We didn't mean to make you mad."

Mom said, "Fun is good, but not when it causes trouble. You have to be careful and respectful of the house and the things in it. You have to clean up after yourselves and ask before you use something. You have to learn to play with what you have, not with what you don't. Now, go to your room and think about what you did. I will clean the bathroom and then we will talk."

Lily and Max went to their room, sad and ashamed. They wished they had not filled the bathroom with balls. They wished they had played peacefully in their room. They learned a lesson that day: playing is fun, but not when it makes a mess.

"What is that?" asked Tom.

"I don't know. Maybe it makes bubbles," said Jen.

They went closer to the machine. They saw a sign that said "Do not touch". But they did not read the sign. They did not know what it meant.

"Let's press the button," said Tom.

"OK," said Jen.

They pressed the button. The machine made a loud noise. It sprayed a lot of water and soap from the hose. It made a lot of foam. The foam was white and fluffy. It looked like fog.

"Wow, this is fun!" said Tom.

"Let's mix the fog with our hands," said Jen.

They ran into the foam. They mixed the fog with their hands. They laughed and shouted. They did not see the pond. They did not see the ducks. They did not see the danger.

The foam was slippery. Tom and Jen slipped on the foam. They fell into the pond. The pond was deep and cold. They could not swim. They could not breathe. They could not call for help. They sank under the water.

The machine stopped. The foam faded. The pond was quiet. The ducks were sad. Tom and Jen were gone.

The moral of the story is: Do not touch things that you do not know. Do not ignore signs that warn you. Do not play near water if you cannot swim. Be careful and listen to your parents. Or you might not be lucky.

Tim and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with their toys, but sometimes they fought. One day, Tim found a big spider in the garden. He thought it was funny and scary. He wanted to tease Sam with it.

He ran to Sam, who was playing with his cars. He said, "Look, Sam, I have a friend for you!" He opened his hand and showed the spider to Sam. Sam was very afraid of spiders. He screamed and ran away. Tim laughed and chased him.

Tim said, "But Mom, it is just a joke. The spider is not alive. It is dead. See?" He put the spider near his mouth and pretended to eat it. He thought it was funny and clever.

But the spider was not dead. It was only sleeping. It woke up when it felt Tim's mouth. It was angry and scared. It bit Tim's tongue. Tim felt a sharp pain. He dropped the spider and cried. He said, "Ow, ow, ow! The spider bit me! It hurts!"

Mom said, "Oh, Tim, I'm sorry. You should not have done that. Come, let me see your tongue. We need to wash it and put some ice on it. Maybe you should go to the doctor. And you should say sorry to Sam. He was not happy with your joke. You should be kind to your brother, not tease him."

Tim said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Sam. I was wrong. I will not tease you again. I don't like spiders either. They are mean and nasty. Can we be friends again?"

Sam said, "It's okay, Tim. I forgive you. But don't do that again. It is not fun. It is scary and dangerous. Let's play with our toys. But not with spiders. They are not toys. They are living things. We should leave them alone."

Mom said, "That's right, boys. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, let's go and have some cookies. But first, let me check your tongue, Tim. I hope it is not too bad."

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their dog, Spot. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. Spot liked to chase the birds and the squirrels. He was a good dog, but sometimes he got very dirty.

"Look at Spot!" Lily said. "He is all muddy and wet. He needs a bath."

They looked around and saw a fountain in the middle of the park. It had a lot of water that sprayed up and down. It looked like fun.

"Let's take Spot to the fountain!" Lily said. "We can wash him there."

"OK, let's go!" Tom said.

They ran to the fountain with Spot. They threw a stick for him to fetch. He ran into the water and came back with the stick. He shook his fur and splashed water everywhere.

"Good boy, Spot!" Tom and Lily said. "You are getting clean."

They did this a few more times. Spot was having a great time. He was not muddy and wet anymore. He was shiny and happy.

But then, they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you kids! Get out of the fountain!" It was a man in a blue shirt. He was the park keeper. He looked very angry. He had a huge broom in his hand.

"Sorry, sir," Tom and Lily said. "We were just washing our dog."

"Well, you can't do that here. This fountain is not for dogs. It is for people to look at and enjoy. You are making a mess. Look at all the water on the ground. And look at my flowers. They are all wet and ruined."

He pointed to the flower beds around the fountain. They were full of water and mud. Some of the flowers were broken and bent.

Tom and Lily felt bad. They did not mean to make a mess. They did not think about the flowers. They just wanted to clean Spot.

"We are sorry, sir," they said. "We did not know. We will not do it again."

The park keeper sighed. He was still angry, but he saw that they were sorry. He decided to give them a chance.

"OK, I will let you go this time. But you have to do something for me. You have to help me clean up this mess. You have to wipe the water and the mud from the ground and the flowers. And you have to say sorry to the flowers. They are living things, too. They need care and respect."

Tom and Lily nodded. They agreed to help the park keeper. They took some cloths and started to wipe the water and the mud. They also said sorry to the flowers. They were gentle and careful.

The park keeper watched them. He saw that they were trying to do a good job. He smiled a little. He was not so angry anymore.

When they finished, the fountain and the flower beds looked better. They were not perfect, but they were cleaner and prettier.

"Thank you, kids," the park keeper said. "You did a good job. You learned your lesson. Next time, if you want to wash your dog, use a hose or a bucket. Not a fountain."

Tom and Lily nodded. They thanked the park keeper. They learned their lesson. They were more careful and respectful.

"Here you go, kids. And here you go, Spot. You are a good dog. You deserve a treat, too."

Tom and Lily smiled. They were happy. They ate their cookies and gave Spot his. He wagged his tail and licked their faces.

One day, Tom sees a new dog in the park. He is big and black and has a red collar. Tom wants to say hello, but the new dog barks at him. He says, "Go away! This is my park. You are not original. You are just a mix of other dogs."

Tom feels sad and angry. He is not a mix. He is original. He has brown fur and blue eyes and a white spot on his tail. He is proud of who he is.

He looks around and sees a flea on the new dog's ear. The flea is small and gray and itchy. Tom has an idea. He runs to the new dog and says, "Hey, I'm sorry. You are right. You are original. Can I be your friend?"

The new dog is surprised. He says, "Really? You want to be my friend?"

Tom says, "Yes, of course. You are so cool and special. Can I come closer and see your red collar?"

The new dog says, "Sure, why not. Come here."

Tom comes closer and pretends to admire the red collar. But he is really looking for the flea. He sees it and quickly snaps it with his teeth. He spits it out and says, "Oops, sorry. I saw a flea on your ear. I wanted to help you."

The new dog feels a sting on his ear. He says, "Ow! That hurt. What did you do?"

Tom says, "I did you a favor. Fleas are bad. They make you scratch and bite. They are not original. They are just a mix of other bugs."

The new dog says, "Oh, I see. Thank you, I guess. You are not so bad after all. Maybe we can be friends."

Tom says, "Sure, why not. We can be friends. But you have to be nice to the other dogs too. They are also original. They have different fur and eyes and spots. They are not a mix. They are themselves."

The new dog says, "OK, I understand. I was wrong. I was mean. I'm sorry. Can you introduce me to your friends?"

Tom says, "Of course. Come on, let's go. They are waiting for us."

Tom and the new dog run to the other dogs. They play and jump and chase balls. They have fun together. They are all original. They are all friends.

Sara and Tom were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they found a big bottle of glue in the closet. They wanted to see what it could do.

"Let's unite our toys with glue!" Sara said. "It will be fun!"

"OK!" Tom said. "I have a car and a bear. You have a doll and a ball. We can make new toys!"

They opened the bottle and poured glue on their toys. They stuck them together and waited. The glue was sticky and wet.

"Look, I made a car-bear!" Tom said. "It has wheels and fur!"

"Wow, I made a doll-ball!" Sara said. "It has hair and bounces!"

They were happy with their new toys. They played with them for a while. Then they wanted to play with their old toys again.

"Let's take the glue off!" Sara said. "I miss my doll and my ball!"

"Me too!" Tom said. "I miss my car and my bear!"

They tried to pull their toys apart. But the glue was strong and dry. They could not separate them. They pulled harder and harder. The toys broke and tore. The glue hurt their fingers and hands.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sara cried. "My doll is ruined! My ball is flat! My fingers are bleeding!"

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "My car is smashed! My bear is ripped! My hands are sore!"

They were sad and angry. They threw their toys away. They blamed each other for the mess.

"It's your fault!" Sara said. "You wanted to unite our toys with glue!"

"No, it's your fault!" Tom said. "You agreed to do it!"

They stopped being friends. They went to their homes and cried. They had no toys and no friends.

The end.

Moral: Glue is not a toy. It can hurt you and your things. Be careful what you unite with glue. You might lose what you love.

One night, Lily and her dad went outside to look at the stars. Lily loved the stars, they were bright and pretty. She wanted to learn their names, but some of them were hard to say.

"Look, Lily, that is a comet!" her dad said, pointing at a streak of light in the sky. "A comet is a big rock that flies very fast and has a tail of fire."

"Wow, a comet!" Lily said, amazed. "Can we catch it, dad?"

Her dad laughed. "No, Lily, comets are too far and too fast for us. But we can make a wish on it. Do you have a wish, Lily?"

Lily thought for a moment. She was shy and did not have many friends at school. She wished she could be more brave and talk to the other kids. But she was afraid to say her wish out loud.

She whispered in her dad's ear. "I wish I could make friends, dad."

Her dad smiled and hugged her. "That is a good wish, Lily. But you know what? You don't need a comet to make it come true. You just need to wipe your fear away and be yourself. You are a smart and kind and funny girl, and I'm sure the other kids will like you if you give them a chance. Why don't you try to say hello to someone tomorrow at school?"

Lily nodded. She felt a little more confident. She looked at the comet again and thanked it for its light. Then she and her dad went back inside and cuddled in bed. Lily fell asleep dreaming of new friends.

They opened the box and saw a lot of old things. There were clothes, books, toys and pictures. They looked like they belonged to someone a long time ago.

Tim and Lily decided to take some things from the box. They thought they were cool and fun. They took a hat, a doll, a car and a book. They did not see the sign on the box that said "Do not touch. These are for the museum. They are very important and rare."

The next day, a man came to the park. He was angry. He was looking for the box. He worked at the museum. He wanted to restore the old things and show them to people. He wanted to tell them the mystery of who owned them and how they lived. He was very sad when he saw the box was empty. He asked the people in the park if they saw anything. No one knew.

Tim and Lily saw the man. They felt guilty. They wanted to give back the things they took. But they were afraid. They thought the man would be mad at them. They hid the things under their beds. They hoped the man would not find them.

But the man did find them. He followed their footprints from the park to their house. He knocked on the door. He asked their mom if he could talk to them. He showed her the sign from the box. He told her what happened. She was shocked. She called Tim and Lily to come downstairs. She asked them if they knew anything about the old things. They nodded. They were scared. They brought the things from their rooms. They gave them to the man. They said they were sorry.

The man looked at the things. He was furious. He saw that the things were damaged. The hat was torn, the doll was dirty, the car was broken and the book was wet. He said they were disgusting. He said they ruined the old things. He said they were very bad and selfish. He said he could not restore them anymore. He said they destroyed the mystery. He said they had to pay for what they did. He took the things and left. He did not forgive them.

Tim and Lily cried. They felt awful. They wished they never took the things from the box. They wished they listened to the sign. They wished they could make the man happy. They learned a hard lesson. They never played in the park again.

Sara shakes her head. She does not like Ben's twist. She thinks he is lying. She wants to stay on Mars. She twists the box again. "No, Ben, we are on Mars!" she says. "The moon is too cold and too boring. Mars is more fun!"

Lila and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were pirates and look for treasure. They had a big box with some shiny things inside. They also had a map that Lila drew with crayons.

"Look, Ben, the map says we have to go to the olive tree. That's where the treasure is!" Lila said.

"Okay, let's go!" Ben said. They ran to the olive tree, which was in the corner of the garden. They saw a cute bird sitting on a branch. It had blue feathers and a yellow beak.

"Hello, bird, do you know where the treasure is?" Lila asked.

"Tweet, tweet, yes, I do. But you have to answer my riddle first," the bird said.

"A riddle? What's that?" Ben asked.

"It's a question that has a funny answer. If you guess right, I'll tell you where the treasure is. If you guess wrong, you have to give me an olive," the bird said.

"Okay, we'll try. What's the riddle?" Lila asked.

"Here it is: What has a face and two hands, but no arms or legs?" the bird said.

Lila and Ben thought hard. They looked at each other and shrugged. They didn't know the answer.

"Can you give us a hint?" Ben asked.

"No, you have to guess. You have ten seconds," the bird said.

Lila and Ben counted to ten. They still didn't know the answer.

"Time's up. What's your guess?" the bird asked.

"Um, a doll?" Lila said.

"No, that's wrong. The answer is a clock. A clock has a face and two hands, but no arms or legs. See?" the bird said, pointing to a clock on the wall of the house.

"Oh, I see. That's a clever riddle," Lila said.

"Yes, it is. Now, give me an olive, please," the bird said.

"Okay, here you go," Ben said, picking an olive from the tree and giving it to the bird.

"Thank you. Now, I'll tell you where the treasure is. It's under the box. You have to lift the box and dig a little bit. There you'll find the treasure," the bird said.

"Really? Thank you, bird. You're very nice," Lila said.

"You're welcome. Have fun, pirates. Bye-bye," the bird said, flying away.

Lila and Ben lifted the box and dug a little bit. They found a small chest with some coins and jewels inside.

"Wow, we found the treasure! We're rich!" Ben said.

"We're rich and smart. We solved the riddle, kind of," Lila said.

They laughed and hugged. They were happy. They decided to share the treasure with the bird and their friends. They settled in the shade of the olive tree and played with their treasure. They had a great day. The end.

Lila was a little fish who liked to swim in the reef. The reef was her home, where she had many friends and saw many colors. She liked to play with the coral, the seaweed and the shells.

One day, a big shark came to the reef. He had sharp teeth and a scary fin. He wanted to eat the little fish. Lila and her friends were very afraid. They hid behind the rocks and the plants. They hoped the shark would go away.

But the shark did not go away. He swam around the reef, looking for food. He saw Lila's tail sticking out from a coral. He opened his mouth and swam fast towards her.

Lila saw the shark coming. She was very scared. She trembled and cried. She wished she could swim away, but she was trapped. She closed her eyes and waited for the end.

But then, something bright flashed in the water. It was a big fish with shiny scales and a long sword. It was a swordfish, and he was Lila's friend. He saw the shark and he was angry. He used his sword to poke the shark in the nose. The shark felt pain and he was surprised. He let go of Lila and swam away.

Lila opened her eyes and saw the swordfish. She was happy and relieved. She thanked him for saving her. He smiled and said he was glad to help. He told her to be careful and to stay with her friends. He swam away, waving his sword.

Lila swam back to her friends. They were happy to see her. They hugged her and said she was brave. They told her they loved her. They played in the reef, feeling safe and happy.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys. Tim has a red motorcycle. Sam has a blue motorcycle. They make vroom-vroom noises and zoom around the room.

One day, they see a big truck outside. The truck has many motorcycles on it. They are shiny and new. Tim and Sam want to see them. They run to the window and look.

"Wow, look at those motorcycles!" Tim says. "They are so cool!"

"I want one!" Sam says. "Can we have one, please?"

They ask their mom. She says no. She says they are too little for real motorcycles. They are sad. They go back to their room.

They look at their toys. They have an idea. They unite their motorcycles. They use tape and string and glue. They make one big motorcycle. It is red and blue. It has four wheels and two seats.

They are happy. They hop on their big motorcycle. They make louder vroom-vroom noises. They zoom around the room.

Their mom hears them. She comes to see. She is alert. She sees their big motorcycle. She smiles.

"That is a very creative motorcycle!" she says. "You are very clever boys!"

Tim and Sam smile. They hug their mom. They say thank you. They keep playing with their big motorcycle. They have fun.

Sam likes to record sounds with his toy phone. He likes to record his mom singing, his dad reading, his dog barking, and his baby sister laughing. He likes to listen to the sounds and pretend he is talking to them.

One day, Sam finds a book about planets in his dad's office. He sees pictures of big balls of different colors and shapes. He learns that some planets are hot, some are cold, some are rocky, and some are gassy. He likes the green planet best. He thinks it looks like a big green apple.

He decides to record the green planet with his toy phone. He holds the phone to the book and says, "Hello, green planet. What is your name? Do you have any friends? What do you like to do?" He waits for an answer, but he hears nothing. He tries again, but still nothing. He gets angry and throws the phone on the floor.

"Sam, what are you doing?" his mom asks, coming into the office. She sees the phone, the book, and Sam's sad face. She picks up the phone and the book and sits next to Sam.

"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to record the green planet, but it won't talk to me. It's not fair. Why won't it talk to me?" Sam says, sniffling.

"Sam, the green planet is not real. It's a picture in a book. It can't talk to you. It's very far away from us, in space. It's not like the sounds you record. They are real. They are from people and animals you know and love. They can talk to you because they are alive and here with you." his mom explains, gently.

Sam looks at his mom and then at the book. He feels silly and confused. He doesn't understand how something can be in a book and not be real. He doesn't understand how something can be so far away and not be here. He doesn't understand how something can be green and not be an apple.

He hugs his mom and says, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know. Can we listen to the sounds I recorded? I like them better. They make me happy."

"Of course, Sam. Let's listen to them together. They make me happy too." his mom says, smiling. She turns on the phone and plays the sounds. They hear his mom singing, his dad reading, his dog barking, and his baby sister laughing. They laugh and sing along. They forget about the green planet and the book. They are happy with the sounds they have.

One day, Sam goes to the park with his mom. He sees a big hill and wants to go down it. He asks his mom if he can. She nods and says, "Be careful, Sam." Sam nods and smiles. He pedals fast and goes down the hill.

But the hill is too steep and Sam loses his balance. He falls off his bike and rolls on the grass. His helmet protects his head, but he feels dizzy. He sees stars and birds around him. He hears his mom calling his name.

She runs to him and hugs him. She asks him if he is okay. He nods and says, "I'm okay, mom." She checks his helmet and his bike. They are both fine. She says, "You are brave, Sam. But next time, choose a smaller hill." Sam nods and says, "Okay, mom." He kisses her and says, "I love you, mom." She says, "I love you, too, Sam." They go home and have some juice and cookies. Sam feels better and tells his mom about his adventure. She listens and smiles.

Tom and Anna are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, and books. But they do not like to share. They always fight over their toys.

One day, Tom sees a colorful ball in Anna's room. He wants to play with it. He sneaks into her room and takes the ball. Anna sees him and gets angry. She runs after him and tries to get the ball back.

"Give me my ball!" Anna shouts. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine now!" Tom says. "I like it!"

They pull and tug on the ball. The ball flies out of their hands and hits a lamp. The lamp falls and breaks. Glass shards fly everywhere. Tom and Anna get scared. They hear their mom coming.

"What happened here?" Mom asks. She sees the broken lamp and the glass. She sees the ball and the toys. She sees Tom and Anna crying.

"We are sorry, Mom," Tom and Anna say. "We were fighting over the ball."

Mom is not happy. She picks up the ball and the toys. She puts them in a big bag. She says, "You two are not careful. You could have hurt yourselves or each other. You do not know how to share. You do not deserve these toys. I will take them to the hospital. There are many children there who have no toys. They will be happy to have them."

Tom and Anna feel sad. They do not want to lose their toys. They do not want to make other children happy. They want to keep their toys for themselves.

Mom takes the bag and leaves. Tom and Anna are left alone in their rooms. They have nothing to play with. They feel bored and lonely. They think about the children in the hospital. They think about how they would feel if they had no toys. They think about how they were selfish and mean.

They decide to go to Mom. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We were wrong. We want to share our toys. We want to make other children happy. Can we go to the hospital with you and give them our toys?"

Mom smiles. She says, "I am glad you changed your minds. You are very kind and generous. Yes, you can come with me and give your toys to the children in the hospital. They will be very grateful and happy. And you will be happy too. Because sharing is caring."

Tom and Anna hug Mom. They get ready to go to the hospital. They hope to make new friends there. They learn a valuable lesson. They learn to share their toys and their love.

Lila and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food for their toys. Lila found a jar of olives in the cupboard and decided to use them for her salad.

"Look, Ben, I have olives for my salad. They are green and round and yummy," she said.

Ben looked at the jar and made a face. He did not like olives. He thought they were unusual and bitter and yucky.

"Yuck, Lila, olives are not yummy. They are bad. I don't want them in my salad," he said.

Lila was hurt by Ben's words. She liked olives and wanted to share them with her brother. She thought he was being rude and mean.

"Ben, olives are not bad. They are good. They provide vitamins and flavor and fun. You should try them. Maybe you will like them," she said.

Ben shook his head. He was stubborn and did not want to try anything new. He pushed the jar away from him and crossed his arms.

"No, Lila, I will not try them. I know I will not like them. You can have them all. I will make my salad with cheese and tomatoes and lettuce," he said.

Lila and Ben started to argue. They raised their voices and said mean things to each other. They forgot about their toys and their fun. They made a mess in the kitchen and made their mom angry.

"Stop, Lila and Ben, stop! What are you doing? Why are you fighting over olives? They are just food. You can like them or not like them, but you don't have to be mean to each other. You are siblings. You should love each other and respect each other's choices. Now, say sorry to each other and clean up this mess," their mom said.

Lila and Ben felt ashamed. They knew their mom was right. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They cleaned up the mess and finished their salads. They gave some olives to their toys and some cheese to their toys. They learned to appreciate each other's differences and to enjoy their food. They had a happy lunch and a happy day.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see the birds.

"Can we climb the tree, please?" Lily asked her mom.

"Be careful, okay? The tree is very high and the branches are thin. Don't go too far," her mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded and ran to the tree. They found a low branch and pulled themselves up. They felt happy and brave. They climbed higher and higher, looking for the birds.

"Look, Lily, I see a nest!" Ben said, pointing to a hole in the tree.

"Wow, let's go see it!" Lily said, following Ben.

They reached the hole and peeked inside. They saw three baby birds with fluffy feathers. They were so cute and tiny. Lily and Ben smiled and said hello to the birds.

But then they heard a loud squawk. It was the mother bird. She was angry and scared. She saw Lily and Ben near her nest. She thought they wanted to hurt her babies. She flew at them with her sharp beak and claws.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily and Ben cried. They felt pain and fear. They tried to get away from the bird, but they lost their balance. They fell from the tree and landed on the ground.

"Help, help, help!" they shouted. Their mom heard them and ran to them. She saw them suffer and bleed. She hugged them and called for help.

The bird saw that Lily and Ben were gone. She calmed down and flew back to her nest. She checked on her babies and saw that they were okay. She was relieved and proud. She sang a song to them and cuddled them.

Lily and Ben were taken to the hospital. They had some cuts and bruises, but they were not badly hurt. They learned a lesson. They should not bother the birds and their nests. They should respect the tree and its life. They should be tidy and safe when they play. They said sorry to the bird and the tree. They hoped they would be friends someday.

Lily was a gifted girl who loved to read and write. She knew many spells and could make things happen with her words. She had a big book of spells that she kept under her bed. She liked to chew on a pencil when she thought of new spells to try.

One day, she wanted to surprise her mom with a spell that would make her happy. She looked in her book and found a spell that said: "Say these words and smile, and you will have a happy day. Rose, sun, cake, hug, joy." Lily thought that sounded nice and easy. She took her pencil and her book and went to the kitchen, where her mom was making breakfast.

"Mom, I have something for you," Lily said. "It's a spell that will make you happy. Can I say it to you?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, honey, I would love to hear your spell. What is it?"

Lily opened her book and read the words: "Rose, sun, cake, hug, joy." As she said each word, she smiled and pointed at something that matched the word. She pointed at a rose in a vase, a sun on the wall, a cake on the table, a hug from her mom, and a joy in her heart.

Her mom was amazed and delighted. She hugged Lily and said, "That's a wonderful spell, my gifted girl. You made me very happy. Thank you so much."

Lily was happy too. She chewed on her pencil and thought of more spells to share with her mom. She didn't know that her pencil was magic too, and that every time she chewed on it, she made a new spell come true. She was about to find out what her next spell would do.

Sara was tired. She had a cold and her nose was runny. Her mom gave her a pill to make her feel better. Sara did not like the pill. It was big and bitter.

"Mom, I don't want the pill. It is yucky," Sara said.

"You have to take the pill, Sara. It will help you get well," her mom said. "Look, I have a scale. We can weigh the pill and see how light it is. Then you can swallow it with some juice."

Sara was curious. She liked the scale. It was shiny and had numbers on it. Her mom put the pill on the scale. It showed one gram.

"See, Sara? The pill is very light. It is only one gram. That is less than a feather. You can take it easily," her mom said.

Sara looked at the pill. It did not look light. It looked hard and nasty. She shook her head.

"No, mom. I don't care how light it is. I don't want the pill. It is yucky," Sara said.

Her mom sighed. She had an idea. She took the pill off the scale and put a grape on it. It showed two grams.

"Look, Sara. The grape is heavier than the pill. It is two grams. That is more than a feather. You like grapes, right? You can eat the grape and then take the pill. It will be easy," her mom said.

Sara looked at the grape. It looked juicy and sweet. She liked grapes. She nodded.

"OK, mom. I will eat the grape and then take the pill. But only if you give me another grape after the pill," Sara said.

Her mom smiled. She gave Sara the grape and the pill. Sara ate the grape and then swallowed the pill with some juice. It was not so bad. She felt proud of herself. Her mom gave her another grape and a hug.

"Good job, Sara. You are a brave girl. The pill will make you feel better soon. Now you can rest and read a book with me," her mom said.

Sara was happy. She liked books. She cuddled with her mom and read a book about a princess and a dragon. She forgot about her cold and her nose. She was not tired anymore. She was glad she took the pill.

"Let's climb up the chimney and look," Ben said. He was older and stronger than Sam.

"No, that's bad," Sam said. He was younger and weaker than Ben. "The chimney is dirty and hot. And maybe there is a fire or a monster inside."

Ben did not listen to Sam. He said, "You are a baby. I am not afraid. I will number how many bricks are in the chimney. Then I will come back down and tell you."

Ben started to climb up the chimney. He put his hands and feet on the bricks and moved up. He counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten..."

Sam watched Ben from the ground. He was worried. He said, "Ben, come back down. It's not safe. You will get hurt."

But Ben did not hear Sam. He kept climbing and counting. He said, "Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty..."

Suddenly, Ben felt something hot and smoky on his face. He looked up and saw a fire in the chimney. He was scared. He said, "Help! Help! Fire! Fire!"

Sam heard Ben scream. He ran to the house and knocked on the door. He said, "Help! Help! My brother is in the chimney. There is a fire. Please help him."

A man opened the door. He saw Sam and heard Ben. He said, "Oh no! What are you doing in the chimney? That's very dangerous. Wait here. I will get a ladder and a hose."

The man got a ladder and a hose. He put the ladder against the chimney and climbed up. He sprayed water on the fire and put it out. He reached down and pulled Ben out of the chimney. He said, "Are you okay, boy? You are very lucky. You could have been burned."

Ben was dirty and coughing. He said, "I'm sorry, sir. I was stupid. I wanted to see what was inside the chimney. I wanted to number the bricks."

The man said, "That was a silly thing to do. You should never go inside a chimney. It's not a place to play. It's a place for smoke and fire. And you should listen to your brother. He was right. He was smart. He was brave. He saved you."

Ben looked at Sam. Sam looked at Ben. Ben said, "Thank you, Sam. You are not a baby. You are my brother. I love you."

Sam said, "I love you too, Ben. But don't ever do that again. Okay?"

Ben said, "Okay."

The man said, "Now, go home and wash up. And be careful next time."

Ben and Sam said, "Yes, sir."

They hugged each other and ran home. They learned a lesson. They never went near a chimney again.

The leopard chuckled to himself and started walking again. As he walked, he thought about the small bird. He realized that sometimes it was nice to take a break and just whistle.

Finally, Tommy was able to catch the mouse. He held it in his hands and felt its soft fur. The mouse was a little scared, but Tommy was extra gentle. He brought the mouse downstairs and put it in an old cardboard box that was heavy.

Afterwards, he sat and watched the mouse explore its new box. The mouse wasn't sure what to do as it scurried around, trying to find a way out. Eventually, the mouse found a tiny hole and slipped out.

Tommy smiled and waved goodbye to the mouse as it scampered away. He had had lots of fun and was excited to search for something else tomorrow!

"Yum, yum, these are so good!" Lila said.

"Let's take some more!" Tom said.

They took some more prunes and put them in their pockets. Then they went back to the garden to play.

But they did not know that the prunes were very old. They had been sitting on the table for a long time, and they had started to rot. Rot means that something is bad and smelly and has germs on it.

As they played, the prunes in their pockets got warmer and softer and more rotten. They also got sticky and messy and stained their clothes.

Soon, they started to smell something bad.

"Yuck, what is that?" Lila asked.

"I don't know, maybe it's the flowers," Tom said.

They sniffed the flowers, but they smelled nice.

"Maybe it's the dirt," Lila said.

They sniffed the dirt, but it smelled normal.

"Maybe it's us," Tom said.

They sniffed each other, and they made a face.

"Ew, it is us!" Lila said.

They looked at their pockets, and they saw the rotten prunes. They were brown and mushy and furry. Furry means that something has hair or fuzz on it. The rotten prunes had white fuzz on them, and that was mold. Mold is a kind of germ that grows on rotten things.

"Yuck, yuck, yuck!" Lila and Tom said.

They threw the rotten prunes away, and they ran to the house. They wanted to wash their clothes and their hands and their faces.

But their mom saw them, and she was not happy.

"What have you done?" she asked. "You took the prunes from the table, and you made a mess!"

She was angry, because the prunes were for the compost. Compost is a pile of old food and leaves and grass that turns into dirt for the garden. The prunes were not for eating, they were for the compost.

Lila and Tom felt sorry, and they said they were sorry.

"We didn't know, mom, we thought they were good," Lila said.

"We like prunes, mom, but not these ones," Tom said.

Mom sighed, and she said they had to learn to ask before they take something. She also said they had to help her clean the mess. She said they could have some fresh prunes later, if they were good.

Lila and Tom nodded, and they said they would. They learned their lesson, and they never took old prunes again. They only took fresh ones, and they always asked first.

One day, Tom and his mom went to the sea. They saw a big boat with many people on it. Mom said, "That is a boat for watching dolphins. Do you want to go and see them?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I like dolphins. They are nice and smart and fast."

Mom and Tom got on the boat and sat on the edge. The boat moved on the water. Tom looked around and saw many waves and birds. He asked, "Mom, where are the dolphins?"

Mom said, "They are in the water, Tom. Sometimes they come up to breathe and play. You have to watch carefully and you will see them."

Tom watched very carefully. He saw a splash and a fin. He pointed and said, "Mom, look! A dolphin!"

Mom looked and said, "Yes, Tom. You are right. That is a dolphin. It is gray and shiny and smooth."

Tom smiled and said, "Can I talk to the dolphin, mom?"

Mom said, "You can try, Tom. Maybe the dolphin will hear you and answer."

Tom leaned over the edge and said, "Hello, dolphin. I am Tom. I like you. Do you want to be my friend?"

The dolphin heard Tom and came closer. It made a sound like a whistle and a click. It jumped out of the water and splashed Tom and mom. Tom laughed and said, "Thank you, dolphin. You are fun. I think you are my friend."

The dolphin nodded and made another sound. It swam around the boat and showed Tom its tail and its teeth. Tom clapped and said, "Wow, dolphin. You are amazing. You can do many things."

Mom said, "Tom, you are lucky. The dolphin likes you. It is very friendly and playful. But we have to go soon. The boat will part and go back to the land."

Tom said, "Oh, mom. I don't want to go. I want to stay with the dolphin."

Mom said, "I know, Tom. But we can't stay here forever. The dolphin has to stay in the water. It has its own family and friends. Maybe we can come back another day and see it again."

Tom said, "Okay, mom. I understand. But can I say goodbye to the dolphin?"

Mom said, "Of course, Tom. You can say goodbye to the dolphin."

Tom waved and said, "Goodbye, dolphin. You are my friend. I will miss you. I hope you are happy and safe."

The dolphin waved back and said, "Goodbye, Tom. You are my friend. I will miss you too. I hope you come back and see me again."

The dolphin gave Tom a big smile and a kiss. Then it dived into the water and swam away. Tom felt sad and happy at the same time. He hugged mom and said, "Mom, that was the best day ever. I love the dolphin. And I love you."

Mom hugged Tom and said, "I love you too, Tom. And I'm glad you had fun with the dolphin. It was a very special day. Now let's go back to the land and tell dad all about it."

Tom and mom got up and went to the other side of the boat. The boat started to move and part from the sea. Tom looked back and saw the water and the sky. He thought of the dolphin and smiled. He said, "Bye, bye, sea. Bye, bye, dolphin. I will see you again."

Mom looks for them. She sees their feet sticking out. She says, "Lily and Ben, come out now. It is time to bathe. You have to wash your body with soap and water. It will make you clean and fresh."

Lily and Ben shake their heads. They say, "No, no, no! We do not like to bathe. It is cold and wet. It makes us cry."

Mom sighs. She says, "Please, Lily and Ben, listen to me. Bathing is good for you. It is fun and relaxing. You can play with your rubber ducks and bubbles. You can sing and splash. You can choose your favorite shampoo and towel. I will help you and hug you."

Lily and Ben peek out from under the sofa. They see Mom's smile. They see the rubber ducks and bubbles. They see the shampoo and towel. They think maybe bathing is not so bad. They say, "OK, Mom, we will bathe. But can we play a little more after?"

Mom nods. She says, "Yes, you can play a little more after. But only if you bathe well and fast. I have a surprise for you. It is something yummy and sweet. But it is only available for a short time. So hurry up and come with me."

Lily and Ben jump out from under the sofa. They follow Mom to the bathroom. They bathe well and fast. They wash their body with soap and water. They play with their rubber ducks and bubbles. They sing and splash. They choose their favorite shampoo and towel. Mom helps them and hugs them.

They feel clean and fresh. They are happy and proud. They say, "Thank you, Mom, for bathing us. We like to bathe now. It is fun and relaxing. What is the surprise you have for us?"

Mom smiles. She says, "You are welcome, Lily and Ben. I am glad you like to bathe now. The surprise I have for you is ice cream. It is your favorite flavor. But it is only available for a short time. So hurry up and get dressed. Then we can go and get some."

Lily and Ben clap their hands. They say, "Yay, ice cream! We love ice cream. It is yummy and sweet. Thank you, Mom, for the surprise. You are the best. We will hurry up and get dressed. Then we can go and get some."

They get dressed quickly. They hold Mom's hand. They go and get some ice cream. They enjoy their treat. They are happy and grateful. They say, "This is the best day ever. We played, we bathed, we ate ice cream. We love you, Mom. You are the best."

Lily likes to write. She writes her name, and her mom's name, and her dad's name. She writes big and small and with many colors. She writes on paper, and on the wall, and on her books.

One day, Lily finds a passport. It is her dad's passport. It has his picture and his name and many stamps. Lily thinks it is a book. She wants to write on it. She takes a red pen and writes "Lily" on the passport.

Her dad sees what she did. He is very angry. He says, "Lily, this is not a book. This is my passport. I need it to go to other places. You cannot write on it. You ruined it." He takes the passport and the pen away from Lily.

Lily is very sad. She says, "I'm sorry, dad. I didn't know. I just wanted to write." She starts to cry.

Her mom hears what happened. She comes to hug Lily. She says, "It's okay, Lily. You made a mistake. You didn't mean to hurt your dad. He is just upset. He loves you very much. He will get a new passport. But you have to be careful. You can only write on things that are for writing. Not on things that are important or belong to someone else."

Lily nods. She says, "I understand, mom. I love you and dad. Can I write you a sorry card?"

Her mom smiles. She says, "Of course, Lily. That would be very nice. But first, let's go and say sorry to your dad. He is in the living room with his hairy friend. He is a dog. He likes to lick and play. Maybe he will make you feel better."

Lily wipes her tears. She says, "Okay, mom. Let's go." She holds her mom's hand and walks to the living room. She sees her dad and his hairy friend. She says, "Sorry, dad. Sorry, hairy friend. Can I pet you?"

Lily loved to zoom on her bike. She had a red bike with a bell and a basket. She liked to ride around the park and say hello to the birds and the flowers. She felt happy and free when she zoomed on her bike.

One day, she saw a boy with a shiny new bike. It was blue and had lights and a horn. It looked very expensive and cool. Lily wanted to see it up close. She zoomed over to the boy and said, "Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?"

The boy looked at her and said, "I'm Max. This is my bike. It's the best bike ever. It can go very fast and make loud noises. Do you want to try it?"

Lily nodded. She was curious about the new bike. She got off her bike and gave it to Max. She climbed on the blue bike and pushed the pedals. It zoomed faster than her red bike. She pressed the horn and it made a loud beep. She felt excited and scared at the same time.

But then, she saw a big dog running towards her. It was barking and growling. It looked angry and hungry. Lily was afraid of the dog. She tried to turn the bike, but it was too heavy and fast. She lost her balance and fell off the bike. She scraped her knee and elbow. She started to cry.

Max ran over to her and helped her up. He said, "Are you okay? I'm sorry, I didn't see the dog. Don't worry, the bike is fine. Here, take your bike back. I don't like it anymore. It's too expensive and hard to ride. I like your bike better. It's simple and fun. Can we be friends?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She said, "Yes, we can be friends. Thank you for letting me try your bike. I'm sorry I fell. I like your bike too, but I love my bike more. It's my life. It makes me happy and free. Do you want to zoom with me?"

Max smiled and nodded. He said, "Yes, I want to zoom with you. Let's go to the park and say hello to the birds and the flowers. Maybe we can find some ice cream too. That would make us feel better."

They got on their bikes and zoomed away. They forgot about the dog and the scrape. They only felt the wind and the sun. They zoomed and laughed and became friends.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play with trains. They have a big track in the playroom. They can make the trains go fast or slow.

One day, Lily and Max have a race. They each pick a train and put it on the track. They say "ready, set, go!" and push the trains. The trains rush on the track. They go around and around.

Lily's train is red. Max's train is blue. Lily's train is faster than Max's train. Lily is happy. She thinks she will win. Max is sad. He thinks he will lose.

Max has an idea. He is smart. He sees a switch on the track. He can change the track. He can make Lily's train go to a different track. He can make his train go to the same track as before.

Max waits for the right time. He sees Lily's train coming. He flips the switch. Lily's train goes to the other track. Max's train stays on the same track. Max's train passes Lily's train. Max is happy. He thinks he will win. Lily is mad. She thinks Max is not fair.

Lily and Max see the end of the track. They see a big bridge. The bridge is broken. There is a gap in the middle. Lily's train is on the track with the bridge. Max's train is on the track without the bridge. Lily is scared. She thinks her train will fall. Max is scared. He thinks he made a bad choice.

Lily and Max yell "stop!" They try to stop their trains. They pull and push. The trains slow down. Lily's train stops before the bridge. Max's train stops after the bridge. Lily and Max are relieved. They are glad their trains are safe.

Lily and Max look at each other. They are sorry. They say "sorry" to each other. They hug. They are friends again. They decide to play with trains together. They do not race. They share the track. They have fun.

"Come on, Ben, let's go on the bridge!" Lily said.

"No, Lily, we can't. Mommy said we have to stay here. The bridge is too far and too high. It is not safe for us," Ben said.

But Lily did not listen to Ben. She was naughty and curious. She ran to the bridge and climbed on the rail. She looked down at the water and saw some ducks. She waved at the ducks and shouted, "Hello, ducks!"

Ben followed Lily and tried to pull her down. He was scared and angry. He said, "Lily, stop! You are being naughty and silly. You could fall and hurt yourself. Mommy will be mad at us. Come down now!"

But Lily did not listen to Ben. She liked to wave at the ducks and see them quack. She said, "No, Ben, I want to stay here. The ducks are my friends. They are waving back at me. Look, they are so cute!"

But the ducks were not waving back at Lily. They were flapping their wings and splashing water. They were trying to tell Lily to go away. They did not like her shouting and waving. They thought she was rude and noisy.

Suddenly, a big truck came on the bridge. It made a loud honk and shook the bridge. Lily lost her balance and fell off the rail. She screamed and cried. Ben grabbed her hand and tried to save her. He screamed and cried too.

Mommy heard their screams and ran to the bridge. She saw Lily and Ben hanging from the rail. She was shocked and scared. She ran to them and pulled them up. She hugged them and checked if they were hurt. She said, "Lily, Ben, are you okay? What were you doing on the bridge? You were very naughty and foolish. You could have died. You made me very worried and sad."

Lily and Ben were sorry and ashamed. They said, "We are sorry, Mommy. We wanted to see the ducks and the other side. We did not mean to be naughty and foolish. We love you, Mommy."

Mommy said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. But you have to listen to me and be careful. The bridge is not a place to play. The ducks are not your friends. They are wild animals. They can bite and hurt you. The other side is not safe for you. There are cars and strangers. You have to stay with me and be good. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We understand, Mommy. We will not go on the bridge again. We will stay with you and be good."

Mommy said, "That's good, Lily and Ben. Now let's go home and have some cookies. You need to rest and calm down. And no more waving at the ducks, okay?"

Lily and Ben said, "Okay, Mommy. No more waving at the ducks."

Anna loved to watch the doves in the park. They were white and soft and made cooing sounds. She wanted to be friends with them, but they always flew away when she came close.

One day, she saw a dove that was hurt. It had a broken wing and could not fly. Anna felt sorry for the dove and wanted to help it. She gently picked it up and carried it to her home. She asked her mom to make a nest for it in a box. She gave it some water and seeds and stroked its feathers.

"Mom, can I keep the dove?" Anna asked.

"No, sweetie, the dove is not a pet. It belongs to the sky. We have to take care of it until it gets better, and then let it go," Mom said.

"Why?" Anna asked.

"Because the dove is a humble bird. It does not want to live in a cage. It wants to be free and fly with its friends. We have to respect that," Mom said.

Anna nodded. She understood. She wanted the dove to be happy. She decided to teach the dove some words, so they could talk to each other. She taught it how to say hello, goodbye, thank you, and I love you. The dove learned quickly and repeated the words after her.

Every day, Anna and the dove played and talked in the box. Anna saw that the dove's wing was healing. It started to flap its wings and hop around. She knew that soon it would be ready to fly again.

One morning, Anna opened the box and saw that the dove was gone. It had flown out of the window. She felt sad, but also proud. She ran to the window and looked for the dove. She saw it in the sky, soaring with the other doves. It looked happy and free.

"Goodbye, dove! Thank you for being my friend! I love you!" Anna shouted.

The dove heard her and turned around. It flew back to the window and landed on the sill. It looked at Anna with its bright eyes and cooed.

"Hello, Anna! Goodbye, Anna! Thank you, Anna! I love you, Anna!" the dove said.

Then it flew away again, but not before giving Anna a gentle peck on the cheek. Anna smiled and waved. She knew that the dove would always remember her, and she would always remember the dove. She had learned a lot from the humble bird. She had learned how to be kind, how to be patient, and how to let go.

Tom was a big cat with a long tail. He liked to chase mice and birds and make them scared. He was fierce and proud of his tail.

One day, he saw a shiny bottle on the grass. It had a label that said "Drink me". Tom was curious and thirsty. He opened the bottle and drank some of the liquid. It tasted sweet and fizzy.

But then, something strange happened. Tom felt his body getting smaller and smaller. He looked at his tail and saw that it was shrinking too. He was no longer a big cat, but a tiny kitten.

"Help! Help!" he cried. "What is happening to me?"

He heard a loud laugh behind him. It was Max, the dog from next door. Max was big and mean and hated cats. He saw Tom and his tiny tail and decided to have some fun.

"Hello, little kitty," Max said. "You look so cute and tasty. I think I will play with you and then eat you."

Tom was terrified. He tried to run away, but Max was faster and stronger. He caught Tom and shook him with his teeth. Tom felt pain and fear. He wished he had never drank from the bottle.

Max was happy. He had caught a cat and made him shrink. He thought it was a funny joke. He did not care that Tom was hurt and sad. He swallowed Tom and his tail in one gulp.

The end.
