The bull looks at Tim and Sue. He says, "Moo. I am sad because I am alone. I have no family. I have no home."

Tim and Sue feel sorry for the bull. They say, "We can be your friends. We can play with you. We can help you find a home."

The bull is happy. He says, "Moo. Thank you, Tim and Sue. You are very kind. You are good friends."

Tim and Sue and the bull play in the park. They have fun. They are happy.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide that was new and shiny. Ben wanted to try it first, but Lily ran faster and got there before him.

"Me first, me first!" Lily shouted as she climbed the ladder. Ben was envious and angry. He wanted to slide too.

"Wait for me, Lily!" Ben said. "It's not fair!"

But Lily did not wait. She slid down the wide slide and laughed. She felt happy and proud. She liked the slide a lot.

Ben was sad and lonely. He did not like the slide anymore. He looked around and saw a swing that was empty and cozy. He decided to enter the swing and push himself. He felt the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He smiled and sang.

Lily saw Ben on the swing and felt curious. She wanted to try the swing too. She left the slide and ran to the swing. But Ben did not let her.

"No, Lily, no!" Ben said. "This is my swing. You have the slide. Go away!"

Lily was envious and angry. She wanted to swing too.

"Please, Ben, please!" Lily said. "Let me swing with you. It's not fair!"

But Ben did not listen. He swung higher and higher and ignored her.

Lily was sad and lonely. She did not like the slide anymore. She looked around and saw a sandbox that was full of toys and friends. She decided to enter the sandbox and play with them. She felt the sand in her hands and the joy in her heart. She giggled and shared.

Ben saw Lily in the sandbox and felt sorry. He wanted to play with her too. He left the swing and walked to the sandbox. But Lily did not see him.

"Hi, Lily, hi!" Ben said. "Can I play with you? I'm sorry I was mean."

But Lily did not hear him. She was busy and happy. She liked the sandbox a lot.

Ben was sad and lonely. He did not like the swing anymore. He looked around and saw nothing that he liked. He wished he had been nicer to Lily. He wished they could play together. He wished they could share the slide, the swing, and the sandbox. He wished they could be twins again.

Sara and Tom were playing on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shells. They saw a big boat on the water. It had a big anchor that hung from a rope.

"Look, Sara, a boat!" Tom said. "Let's go see it!"

They ran to the water and saw the anchor closer. It was shiny and heavy. Sara wanted to touch it.

"Can I touch the anchor, Tom?" Sara asked.

"OK, but be careful. It might be sharp or dirty," Tom said.

Sara reached out her hand and touched the anchor. It felt cold and hard. She liked it. She wanted to take it home.

"Tom, can we take the anchor home?" Sara asked.

"No, Sara, we can't. It belongs to the boat. The boat needs it to stay in one place. If we take it, the boat will drift away," Tom said.

"But I like it. It's pretty. Please, Tom, please," Sara begged.

Tom looked around. He saw that the boat was far away and no one was watching. He was curious about the anchor too. He thought it would be fun to play with it.

"OK, Sara, but only for a little while. We have to bring it back soon," Tom said.

He helped Sara lift the anchor. It was very heavy. They dragged it to the sand. They played with it for a while. They pretended it was a treasure or a weapon or a toy.

They were so busy playing that they did not notice the wind and the waves. They did not hear the boat's horn. They did not see the boat's owner. He was angry and scared. He saw that his anchor was gone. He saw that his boat was moving. He shouted and waved his arms.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing with my anchor? Give it back! Give it back now!" he yelled.

Sara and Tom heard him. They looked up and saw him. They were scared too. They did not know he was there. They did not know they did something bad.

"Sorry, mister, sorry. We just wanted to play. We'll give it back. We'll give it back now," they said.

They tried to lift the anchor again. But it was too heavy. They could not move it. The sand was wet and sticky. The anchor was stuck.

"Help, help. We can't move it. Help, help," they cried.

The boat's owner ran to them. He was very angry. He grabbed the rope and pulled the anchor. He pulled and pulled. He was strong. He freed the anchor. He dragged it to the water. He threw it back to the boat.

He looked at Sara and Tom. He was still angry. He did not thank them. He did not forgive them. He scolded them.

"You kids are very naughty. You almost made me lose my boat. You could have hurt yourselves or someone else. You should not touch things that are not yours. You should not play with dangerous things. You should listen to your parents. Where are they? I'm going to tell them what you did," he said.

He took Sara and Tom by the hand. He walked them to the beach. He looked for their parents. He found them. They were sitting on a blanket. They were reading and talking. They did not see what happened. They did not know what their kids did.

The boat's owner told them. He told them everything. He was very loud. He was very mad.

Sara and Tom's parents were shocked. They were ashamed. They were sorry. They apologized to the boat's owner. They thanked him for saving his boat. They thanked him for bringing their kids back. They did not thank their kids. They did not praise their kids. They punished their kids.

They scolded Sara and Tom. They took away their toys. They made them sit on the blanket. They did not let them play anymore. They did not let them have fun anymore.

Sara and Tom were sad. They were sorry. They did not mean to do something bad. They just wanted to play. They just liked the anchor. They learned their lesson. They never touched an anchor again.

Lily likes to touch books. She likes to see the pictures and hear the sounds of the words. She has many books in her room, but her favorite one is a book of poems. Poems are like songs, but you do not sing them, you read them.

One day, Lily's mom gave her a new book of poems. It was a big and colorful book, with many poems inside. Lily was very happy and thanked her mom. She opened the book and started to read the first poem. It was about a dragon who liked to eat spicy food.

"Spicy food makes me breathe fire," the dragon said. "I like to roast marshmallows and popcorn with my fire. But sometimes I eat too much and my tummy hurts. Then I drink some water and feel better."

Lily laughed at the poem. She liked the dragon and his fire. She wondered what spicy food tasted like. She asked her mom, "Mom, what is spicy food?"

"Spicy food is food that has a strong and hot flavor," her mom explained. "Some people like it, and some people do not. Do you want to try some spicy food?"

Lily nodded. She was curious and brave. Her mom gave her a small piece of pepper. Lily touched it with her tongue. It was very spicy! She felt a tingling and burning sensation in her mouth. She made a funny face and said, "Ouch! Spicy food is too spicy for me!"

Her mom smiled and gave her a glass of milk. Lily drank the milk and felt better. She said, "I think I like poems better than spicy food. Can we read more poems, mom?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "Of course, my sweet Lily. Let's read more poems together." They cuddled on the couch and read more poems from the book. Lily liked to touch the words and hear the sounds. She felt happy and warm.

Lily fell on the candle and her hair caught fire. Mira screamed and ran to her mom. Her mom heard her and came to the table. She saw Lily burning and quickly put out the fire. She took Mira and Lily and hugged them.

Mira was very sorry and sad. She hurt her hand and Lily. Her mom told her not to touch candles. They were dangerous and could burn things. She also told her that Lily was still her doll and she loved her. She said they could fix Lily's hair and dress.

One day, Sara saw a bottle on the shelf. It said "Flea Spray". Sara thought this was the answer. She took the bottle and went to find Spot. She did not ask her mom or dad. She was naughty.

Spot was sleeping on his bed. Sara sprayed him with the flea spray. Spot woke up and yelped. He did not like the spray. It smelled bad and stung his eyes. He ran away from Sara. He was angry and scared.

Sara felt sorry. She did not mean to hurt Spot. She wanted to make him happy. She followed him and said, "Spot, come back! I'm sorry! I love you! You are my best friend!"

Spot heard Sara. He stopped and looked at her. He saw that she was sad. He wagged his tail. He loved Sara too. He knew that she valued him. He forgave her. He went back to her and licked her face.

Sara hugged Spot. She said, "I'm sorry, Spot. I won't spray you again. I'll ask mom or dad to help you with the fleas. You are a good dog. You are my best friend too!"

They often quarreled over who got the best spot on the sofa, or who got to play with the red ball, or who got to drink from the faucet.

One day, the human brought home a big box. Lila and Ben were curious and went to see what was inside. They smelled something new and strange. They heard a tiny meow. They peeked inside and saw a small, fluffy kitten. The human said, "This is Molly. She is your new sister. Be nice to her, okay?"

Lila and Ben did not like Molly. They thought she was too small and too cute and too noisy. They did not want to share their food and toys and warm places with her. They hissed and growled and scratched at her. Molly was scared and sad. She hid under the bed and cried.

The human was not happy. He said, "Lila and Ben, you are being very mean. Molly is part of our family now. You have to be kind and gentle and play with her. If you don't, I will have to find another home for you."

Lila and Ben did not want to leave their big house and their nice human. They did not want to lose their food and toys and warm places. They did not want to be alone. Molly was surprised and happy. She came out from under the bed and rubbed her nose against Lila and Ben. She said, "Thank you. I want to be your friends too. I have a lot to learn from you. Can you show me the sofa and the red ball and the faucet?"

Lila and Ben smiled and nodded. They took Molly to their favorite spots and shared their toys and water. They played and cuddled and purred. The human was glad and proud. He said, "That's my good cats. You are a happy family now." He gave them all a hug and a treat and a warm place to sleep.

One day, Ben and Sam want to play chess by themselves. They split the pieces in half. Ben takes the black pieces and Sam takes the white pieces. They put the pieces on the board.

"Let's play!" Ben says.

"OK!" Sam says.

They start to move the pieces. Ben moves his knight. Sam moves his pawn. Ben moves his bishop. Sam moves his queen.

"Check!" Sam says. He smiles. His queen is near Ben's king.

"What happened?" Dad asks.

Dad shakes his head. He is not happy. He picks up the pieces and the board.

"Chess is a fun game. But you have to play nice. You have to respect the pieces and your brother. You have to say sorry when you make a mistake. You have to say good game when you finish. Do you understand?" Dad says.

Ben and Sam look at each other. They feel sorry. They nod.

"Sorry, Sam." Ben says.

"Sorry, Ben." Sam says.

"Good. Now, let's play chess together. I will teach you some tricks." Dad says.

But the dragon was very big and strong, and Max's car was very small and weak. The dragon knocked the car over with his tail, and Max fell to the floor.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Max shouted, rubbing his head. "That hurt!"

The dragon roared and moved closer to Lily and her doll. Lily was scared, and she didn't know what to do.

"Please, dragon, don't hurt us!" Lily begged. "We are sorry for playing in your cave. We will go away and leave you alone. Please, please, please!"

The dragon looked at Lily and her doll. He saw that they were very small and sweet, and he felt sorry for them. He decided to be nice and let them go.

"Okay, okay, okay," the dragon said. "You can go. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will never come back to my cave again. And you have to promise me that you will always be kind and share your toys with others. Do you promise?"

Lily and Max nodded their heads. They were happy that the dragon was not angry anymore. They said thank you to the dragon, and they ran to the door.

"Bye, bye, dragon!" they said. "We promise, we promise, we promise!"

The dragon smiled and waved his tail. He was glad that he had made some new friends. He hoped that they would keep their promise and be good.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that sometimes it is better to surrender and be polite than to fight and be rude. It also teaches that kindness can make friends out of enemies.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The story sets up the contrast between Lily and Max's toys and the dragon's size and strength, which pays off when the dragon easily defeats Max's car. It also foreshadows the dragon's change of heart when he looks at Lily and her doll, which pays off when he lets them go and asks them to be kind and share.

She saw something shiny in the hole. It looked like a coin. She wanted to have it, so she went inside the hole.

The hole was not a cave. It was a trap. It had a door that closed when Lily went inside. Lily was trapped in the hole. She could not get out. She could not see anything. She could not hear anything. She could not breathe. She cried and cried, but no one came. She vanished in the hole. The end.

Sarah thanked Timmy for reminding her to be safe. 

Later that day, Timmy was playing with his toy cars when he accidentally knocked over a vase. Sarah came to help him clean up the mess. Timmy was feeling a little clumsy, but Sarah told him it was okay and that accidents happen. They worked together to clean up the broken pieces and put them in the garbage. 

After they were done cleaning, Timmy and Sarah went for a bike ride. Timmy was so happy to have a big sister who looked out for him and taught him how to be safe. He knew he could always count on her to help him when he was feeling clumsy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the kitchen with her mommy. One day, they were making cookies together when Lily found a bug on the counter. She said, "Mommy, what's that bug?" Her mommy said, "Let's examine it and see." They looked at the bug and saw that it was a little beetle. 

Lily said, "Wow, it's so lively!" Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's moving around a lot." Lily wanted to keep the beetle as a pet, but her mommy said it needed to go back outside to be with its family. 

Later that day, Lily and her mommy went outside to play. Lily saw some ants crawling on the ground and said, "Mommy, let's examine these ants too!" They watched the ants for a while and then went back inside to finish making their cookies. It was a fun and lively day in the kitchen with Lily and her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a big ostrich named Olly. Olly was pale and fast. He lived in a big field with his friends. They liked to run and play all day. The sun was bright and they were happy.

One day, Olly and his friends saw a ball. They wanted to play catch with it. But they did not know how. They tried to use their beaks, but the ball fell down. Olly was sad. He wanted to play catch with his friends.

A small bird named Benny saw Olly and his friends. Benny knew how to play catch. He showed Olly and his friends how to catch the ball with their wings. They tried and tried, and soon they could catch the ball too. Olly and his friends were so happy. They played catch all day long.

The moral of the story is that we can always learn new things from others, even if they are different from us.

The kangaroo wanted to help, so he picked up the box with his thick tail. He hopped and hopped, carrying the box. He saw a big tree and knew he was close to the other side of the forest.

The kangaroo kept hopping until he found a small house. He put the box down and knocked on the door. A little girl opened the door and saw the box. She was very happy.

But when the little girl opened the box, there was nothing inside. The kangaroo was sad. He thought he had done a good job, but the box was empty. The little girl said, "Thank you, kangaroo, but there is nothing here for me." The kangaroo hopped away with a heavy heart, feeling like he had failed.

Then they come to the fruit and vegetable section. Mom says they need to get some broccoli. Jen and Tom do not like broccoli. They think it is green and yucky. They make a face and say no. Mom says broccoli is good for them. It makes them strong and healthy. She says they can have a treat if they eat some broccoli at home.

Jen and Tom think about it. They like treats. They like cookies, ice cream, and candy. They want to have a treat. They decide to try some broccoli. They put some broccoli in their carts. Mom smiles and says they are good kids.

They go to the cashier and pay for their things. They say hello to the cashier. He is a jolly man. He has a big beard and a red hat. He gives them each a sticker. They say thank you and bye. They go back to the car and drive home.

At home, Mom cooks the broccoli. She adds some cheese and butter. She says it will make it tasty. She gives Jen and Tom a plate with some broccoli and some chicken. Jen and Tom look at the broccoli. They are not sure. They take a small bite. They are surprised. It is not so bad. It is cheesy and buttery. They take another bite. They like it. They eat all their broccoli and their chicken. Mom is proud of them. She gives them each a cookie. They are happy. They say broccoli is not so bad. They say they will eat it again. Mom hugs them and says they are jolly kids. They hug her back and say they love her. They have a good day.

Lily and Tom waited in the living room. They played with their toys and books, but they were hungry and bored. They looked at the cake on the table. It smelled so good.

"I want some cake now," Tom said. "Just a little bit. Mom won't notice."

"No, Tom. We have to wait. It's not fair to eat the cake before everyone else," Lily said.

Lily followed him. She saw him reach for the knife. She tried to stop him.

"Tom, don't! You'll ruin the cake!" she said.

Tom ignored her. He cut a big slice of cake and put it on a plate. He licked his lips and smiled.

"Yum, yum. This is the best cake ever," he said.

Lily was angry and sad. She saw the hole in the cake. It looked pale and ugly. She felt tears in her eyes.

"Tom, you're so mean! You spoiled the cake! Mom will be mad at you!" she said.

Tom shrugged. He didn't care. He ate the cake and made a mess.

"Who cares? It's just cake. And it's delicious. Do you want some?" he said.

He offered the plate to Lily. He hoped she would accept and stop crying.

Lily looked at the plate. She saw the crumbs and the frosting. She felt hungry and tempted. But she also felt hurt and betrayed.

She shook her head. She pushed the plate away.

"No, thank you. I don't want your cake. You're a bad brother. I don't like you," she said.

She ran to the couch and buried her face in a pillow. She sobbed and waited for mom to come.

Lila and Ben are playing in the park. They like to swing and slide and run. They see a big hill with a flag on top. They want to climb the hill and see the flag.

"Let's go to the flag, Ben!" Lila says. "Maybe we can see the west from there."

"What is the west, Lila?" Ben asks.

"The west is where the sun goes when it is night. It is very far and pretty. My mom told me." Lila says.

They start to climb the hill. It is hard and steep. They hold hands and help each other. They see rocks and flowers and bugs. They are almost at the top when they hear a loud noise.

"Boom!" It is thunder. They look up and see dark clouds. It is going to rain.

"Oh no, Ben! We have to go back! It is not safe here!" Lila says.

They turn around and run down the hill. They are scared and wet. They see a big tree. They run to the tree and hide under it.

"Are you okay, Lila?" Ben asks.

"I am okay, Ben. Are you okay?" Lila asks.

"I am okay, Lila. But I am cold and wet." Ben says.

They hug each other and shiver. They see a flash of light. It is lightning. It strikes the flag on the hill. The flag burns and falls.

"Wow, Lila! Did you see that? The lightning struck the flag!" Ben says.

"I saw that, Ben. It was scary and loud. The flag is gone." Lila says.

They hear a voice. It is Lila's mom. She is looking for them.

"Lila! Ben! Where are you?" She calls.

"Here, mom! Here!" Lila and Ben shout.

Lila's mom sees them under the tree. She runs to them and hugs them.

"Thank goodness, you are safe! What are you doing here? It is stormy and dangerous!" She says.

"We wanted to see the flag, mom. We wanted to see the west. But the storm came and the lightning struck the flag. We were scared, mom." Lila says.

"I am sorry, Lila. I know you were curious. But you should not go to the hill when it is stormy. It is not useful. It is risky. You could get hurt. You should stay close to me and listen to me. I love you and I want you to be safe." Lila's mom says.

"I am sorry, mom. I love you too. I will listen to you next time." Lila says.

Lila's mom smiles and kisses them. She wraps them in a blanket and takes them to the car. She drives them home. They are warm and dry. They are happy and safe. They learned a lesson. They will not go to the hill when it is stormy. They will wait for a sunny day. Then they will try to see the west again. Maybe they will see the flag too.

One day, Sam and his dad are playing chess in the living room. Sam is very focused and wants to win. He moves his queen and says "check". His dad smiles and says "good move, Sam". But then, Sam hears a loud noise from outside. He looks out the window and sees a big truck. The truck is very noisy and makes Sam's ears hurt. He does not like the truck.

Sam wants the truck to go away. He says "shoo, shoo, truck". But the truck does not listen. It keeps making noise and blowing smoke. Sam gets angry and starts to cry. He does not want to play chess anymore. He throws his pieces on the floor and runs to his mom. He says "mom, make the truck stop".

His mom hugs him and says "it's okay, Sam. The truck is just doing its job. It will leave soon. Don't be mad at the truck. It does not know you are playing chess". She takes him to the kitchen and gives him a glass of milk and a cookie. She says "why don't you calm down and then go back to your dad? He is waiting for you to finish the game".

Sam drinks his milk and eats his cookie. He feels better. He says "sorry, mom. I was rude to the truck". His mom says "that's okay, Sam. I'm glad you are sorry. Now, go and say sorry to your dad too. He loves you and wants to play with you". Sam nods and goes back to the living room. He sees his dad picking up the pieces and setting up the board. He says "sorry, dad. I was mad at the truck. Can we play again?". His dad says "of course, Sam. I'm happy you are back. Let's play again. And don't worry about the truck. It will be gone soon". He gives Sam a hug and a kiss. They sit down and resume their game. Sam manages to checkmate his dad and wins. He says "yay, I did it". His dad says "well done, Sam. You are a smart and brave chess player". They both laugh and clap. They are happy. The truck leaves and the noise stops. The end.

Lily said, "No, Tom, don't do that. That is a stupid idea. The branch is already shiny enough. If you polish it, you will make it slippery and fall off."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He said, "You are silly, Lily. I know how to polish things. I will use this cloth and rub the branch hard. Then it will be the best branch ever." He took a cloth from his pocket and started to polish the branch.

Lily watched Tom and shook her head. She said, "Tom, stop it. You are making a mistake. The branch is not safe. You will hurt yourself." But Tom did not stop. He polished the branch faster and faster. He said, "Look, Lily, look how shiny the branch is. It is so pretty. I am the best polisher in the world."

Tom was so proud of his work that he did not notice that the branch was getting very slippery. He tried to swing on the branch, but his hands slipped and he lost his grip. He fell off the branch and landed on the ground. He hit his head and his arm and started to cry. Lily ran to him and tried to help him. She said, "Tom, Tom, are you okay? I told you not to polish the branch. You were stupid and now you are hurt."

"Wow, look at that!" Tim says.

"It's a bird and her babies!" Anna says.

The bird sees them and stops making the sound. She looks at them with her black eyes. She does not seem scared or angry. She seems curious and friendly.

"Hello, kids," the bird says.

Tim and Anna are surprised. They did not know that birds can talk.

"How can you talk?" Anna asks.

"Thank you, Dad!" Lily and Ben say.

"You're welcome, kids. But you should remind Max not to jump into the river. It's dangerous," Dad says.

They hug Max and dry him with a towel. Mom smiles and gives them a hug too.

"Good job, kids. You were brave and smart. You didn't go too close to the water. You called for help. You did the right thing," Mom says.

Lily and Ben feel proud and happy. They love their family and their dog. They love the park and the river. But they don't love the modern boat. It's too loud and scary. They prefer the old boats. They are quiet and nice.

Tommy thought for a moment. He did want to be a big boy. He wanted to make his mom and his teacher proud. He wanted to learn and grow. But he also wanted to have fun and be himself.

"Mom, can I be a big boy and still play with my toys and watch cartoons?" he asked.

"Of course, Tommy," his mom said. "You can do both. But you have to balance your time. You have to study first, then play. And you have to get haircuts once in a while, but you can choose how you want your hair to look. How about that?"

Tommy nodded. He felt better. He decided to study harder and get better grades. He also decided to keep his hair a little longer and style it with some gel. He thought he looked cool and smart. He hugged his mom and thanked her for the haircut. He was a big boy, but he was still Tommy.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play hide and seek. One day, they decided to play in the big park near their house. Ben said, "I will count to ten and you hide. Then I will find you." Lily nodded and ran away.

Ben closed his eyes and counted. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Ready or not, here I come!" He opened his eyes and looked around. He saw a big tree with a hole in it. He thought, "Maybe Lily is hiding in there." He walked towards the tree.

But Lily was not hiding in the tree. She was hiding behind a bush. She saw Ben go to the tree and smiled. She thought, "He will never find me here." She waited for him to give up and come back.

But Ben did not give up. He reached the tree and peeked inside the hole. He saw something furry and brown. He thought, "Is that Lily's hair?" He reached his hand inside the hole and touched it. It was soft and warm. He said, "I found you, Lily!"

But it was not Lily's hair. It was a bear's nose. The bear was sleeping in the tree and did not like to be disturbed. It woke up and roared. It bit Ben's hand and pulled him inside the hole. Ben screamed and cried. He wished he had recognized the bear's nose.

Lily heard Ben's scream and ran to the tree. She saw blood and fur. She was scared and sad. She wished she had been wise and not hidden so far. She called for help, but no one came. She was alone with the bear.

Tom and Mia liked to play hide and seek in the park. They ran and laughed and had fun. One day, they saw a big zoom on the road. It was red and shiny and made a loud noise. Tom and Mia wanted to see it closer.

They ran to the road, but they did not look for cars. They did not hear their mom call them to stop. They only saw the big zoom. They thought it was a toy.

But the big zoom was not a toy. It was a fire truck. It was going to a fire. It was in a hurry. It did not see Tom and Mia. They did not see it either. They were too busy hiding behind a bush.

The fire truck zoomed past the bush. It hit Tom and Mia. They screamed and fell. They were hurt. They were not alert. They did not play anymore. Their mom ran to them. She cried and hugged them. She called for help. But it was too late. Tom and Mia were gone. The big zoom took them away.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom. One day, they see a large truck in the park. The truck has many boxes and a big lock on the back.

"Wow, look at that truck!" Tom says. "I wonder what is inside the boxes."

"Maybe toys, or candy, or books," Lily says. "Can we go and see, mom?"

Mom shakes her head. "No, we can't. The truck belongs to someone else. We have to respect their things. We can watch from here, but we can't touch."

Lila nodded and said, "You are right. I was foolish and reckless. I will hop back to my mama and say sorry. And I will never hop to a new place without her permission again."

They open the door. They go out. They close the door. They lock it. They throw the key away.

They never go back to the secret place. They never talk about it. They forget about it.

They play in the big house. They play with their toys, their books, their beds. They play with their friends. They have fun.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big melon on a table. It was green and round and looked yummy.

"Let's take it and eat it," Sara said.

"No, that's not ours. It belongs to someone else," Ben said.

But Sara did not listen. She ran to the table and grabbed the melon. She tried to run away, but the melon was too heavy. She dropped it on the ground and it broke into pieces.

"Oh no!" Sara cried.

Just then, a lady came out of a nearby house. She saw Sara and the broken melon. She was angry.

"Hey, you! What did you do to my melon? That was for my picnic!" she shouted.

Sara felt very embarrassed. She wanted to hide. She looked at Ben for help, but he was shaking his head.

"I'm sorry, lady. I was hungry and I wanted to try it," Sara said.

The lady sighed. She saw that Sara was just a little girl who made a mistake. She decided to be kind.

"Well, you should have asked first. But I guess you learned your lesson. Here, have a slice of the melon. It's very sweet and juicy," she said.

She gave Sara and Ben each a piece of the melon. They thanked her and ate it. It was delicious.

The lady smiled. She thought Sara and Ben were adorable, even if they were naughty. She invited them to join her picnic. They agreed and had a fun time. They made a new friend and learned to be polite. They never took things that were not theirs again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the living room. They had many toys and books, but they were bored. They wanted to do something new and fun.

"Look, there is a fireplace!" Tom said, pointing to the corner. "Let's pretend we are camping and make a fire."

"OK, but how?" Lily asked. She had never seen a real fire before.

Tom looked around and saw some paper and matches on the table. He had an idea. He took some paper and tore it into pieces. He put them in the fireplace and took a match.

"Watch this!" he said, and struck the match on the box. It made a bright spark and a flame. He threw the match into the paper and smiled.

"Wow, you made a fire!" Lily said, clapping her hands. She moved closer to the fireplace and felt the warmth.

But soon, the fire grew bigger and bigger. The paper was not enough. The fire started to catch the wood and the carpet. Smoke filled the room and made them cough.

"Help, help!" Lily shouted, scared. "The fire is too big! It will burn everything!"

Tom was scared too. He did not know what to do. He dropped the matches and ran to the door. He tried to open it, but it was locked. He banged on it and yelled for help.

"Help, help! There is a fire! Let us out!"

Lily followed him and cried. She hugged him and hoped someone would hear them.

Outside, their mom and dad were coming back from the store. They saw smoke coming out of the window and heard their children's voices. They ran to the door and tried to open it, but it was locked too.

"Tom, Lily, are you OK?" their mom shouted, worried. "We are here, we will help you!"

She took a key from her pocket and unlocked the door. She opened it and saw the fire in the living room. She grabbed a blanket and threw it over the fire. She put it out and stopped the smoke.

Their dad rushed in and picked up Tom and Lily. He hugged them and checked if they were hurt. They were not, but they were very scared and sorry.

"Mom, dad, we are sorry!" Tom said, sobbing. "We wanted to play with the fireplace, but we made a big fire. We did not mean to!"

"We are sorry too!" Lily said, sniffling. "We did not know it was dangerous. We were bored and curious."

Their mom and dad were angry and relieved. They were angry that their children had played with matches and fire, but they were relieved that they were safe and sound.

"Tom, Lily, you were very naughty and foolish!" their mom said, sternly. "You could have burned the house and yourselves! You should never play with matches and fire! They are not toys, they are dangerous!"

"We know, mom, we know!" Tom and Lily said, nodding. "We are sorry, we are sorry!"

Their dad said, softly, "We are glad you are OK, but you have to learn from this. You have to listen to us and follow the rules. You have to be careful and responsible. You have to respect the fireplace and the things in the house. Do you understand?"

"Yes, dad, we understand!" Tom and Lily said, looking down. "We will not do it again, we promise!"

Their mom and dad hugged them and kissed them. They were still angry, but they loved them very much. They took them to the kitchen and gave them some water and cookies. They talked to them and explained why fire was dangerous and how to use the fireplace safely. They also told them that they would have to clean the living room and fix the damage. They would have to work hard and help each other.

Tom and Lily agreed and said they were sorry again. They felt bad for what they had done. They also felt lucky that their mom and dad had helped them. They realized that the fireplace was not a toy, but a useful and beautiful thing. They decided to never play with fire again, and to always listen to their mom and dad. They also decided to find other ways to have fun and be creative, without being naughty and foolish. They learned a big lesson that day.

Suddenly, an idea came to his mind. He reached for the broom. Then he stuck the broom handle between the shelf and the ashtray and tried to pull it down. He shook the broom back and forth, but the ashtray remained stuck. He shook harder, but it was no use. The ashtray was too heavy and too hard on the shelf.

The man looked around and found a box. He placed the box on the chair and then climbed on top of it. He tried again to reach the ashtray. This time, his fingers were just able to touch it. He pushed the ashtray and it fell to the ground.

The man smiled. He had finally reached the ashtray. He stepped off the chair and the box and picked up the ashtray from the floor. He was so happy he had done it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old, and he loved to play outside. 
One day, he was running around in his yard when he heard a loud noise. He frowned. He looked up and realized it was two birds fighting in the sky. It made Joe sad. He wanted peace.

Joe's dad saw he was frowning and gave him a hug. He softly said, "We need to make peace, Joe."

Joe and his dad went to the store to buy peace. When they arrived, they saw a jar of honey. Joe smiled and reached for it. His dad said, "No, this is too sweet for peace. We need something less sweet and more bitter." 

So Joe's dad bought a jar of vinegar and said, "This will make peace bitter, but it's the right sweet-bitter mix for making peace."

The family went home and mixed the vinegar and honey together. Joe saw the mixture turn a beautiful color and smiled. His dad said, "Joe, now we have peace!" Joe frowned while he thought of all the birds fighting. 

He knew that peace can be sweet, but sometimes it also needs to be a bit bitter to stand a chance.

There once was a modest oak tree. A family of squirrels lived in its branches. Every day, they would frolic and play beneath its wide shadow.

One day, the family of squirrels was startled by a loud rumbling. It was unlike anything they had ever heard before, and it seemed to be growing louder and closer. Suddenly, an enormous truck stopped near their home, and a family began to unload something from the back.

The squirrels watched in curiosity as the family began to raise a large tent in the empty field next to the oak tree. Before long, the tent was raised, and the family began raising colorful flags and banners on tall poles. This made the squirrels even more curious.

Over the next few weeks, the family continued to prepare the field and eventually held a big festival. Everyone from far and wide gathered to celebrate the special event. The squirrels stayed nearby, in their home of the oak tree, chattering away and watching in awe.

By the end of the festival, the family had raised enough money to make their modest dreams a reality. What began as a simple oak tree now provided a safe home and prosperity to a large family of squirrels.

Jimmy asked his mom, "Mom, why is the butterfly so stubborn?" Mom laughed and said, "Well, the butterfly is stubborn because it wanted to stay in the park and can't seem to fly away!" Jimmy waved goodbye as he and his mom walked away. He knew he would never forget this peaceful and stubborn butterfly.

The dragon was about to eat the page, when a brave knight came to save him. The knight was wearing a shiny suit of armor, and he had a big sword in his hand. He jumped into the river and fought the dragon. After a long battle, the brave knight was able to save the page.

The page thanked the knight for saving it. The knight said, "No problem. It is always best to help those in need". From that day on, the page was never scared or spoiled again. It was safe, and it had a new friend in the brave knight.

Lily stopped just in time and did not fall. She took the pot off her head and put it back in the kitchen. From that day on, she always looked where she was going when she played. And she never used the pot as a hat again.

They decided to show the fancy bottle to their wise old friend, Mr. Turtle. Mr. Turtle told them that wine was for grown-ups, not little fish like them. Fin and his friends listened to Mr. Turtle and continued to swim and play, leaving the fancy bottle behind. They knew that they could have fun without it.

When Tim was all clean, he put on his pajamas and went to the kitchen. The pie was ready! Tim and his mom sat down and ate the delicious pie together. They both loved it and Tim felt happy that he did something different that day.

Tom and Sam drove around in the big gray van. They looked high and low for the red ball. Finally, they saw it under a tree. Sam was so happy to gain his red ball back. Tom was happy too because he helped Sam. They both went home in the big gray van, smiling and laughing.

One day, a small dog named Spot went for a walk in the park. He saw a big tree with lots of red apples. Spot wanted to eat an apple, but they were too high for him to reach. He jumped and jumped, but he could not get one.

Then, a tall giraffe named Gerry walked by. Spot asked, "Can you help me get an apple, please?" Gerry smiled and said, "Sure, little friend!" Gerry stretched his long neck and picked an apple for Spot.

Spot was so happy. He used his teeth to bite into the apple. It was sweet and juicy. As a reward for helping him, Spot shared his apple with Gerry. They both enjoyed the tasty treat and became good friends. From that day on, they always played together in the park.

Once upon a time, there was an honest boy named Tim. He had a red cap that he loved very much. One day, while playing outside, he saw a big box. The box had a lock on it.

Tim wanted to open the lock, but he did not have a key. He tried to pull and push, but the lock did not open. He was sad and sat down near the box, still wearing his red cap.

Just then, a kind squirrel came by and saw Tim. The squirrel said, "I have a key to open the lock!" Tim was very happy. The squirrel opened the lock, and inside the box, they found lots of toys. Tim and the squirrel played with the toys all day long, and they became good friends.

One day, in an ordinary little town, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily liked to play outside in the evening. One evening, while she was playing, she saw a cat. The cat was very cute and Lily wanted to pet it.

"Hi, cat! Can I pet you?" Lily asked. The cat nodded and Lily petted it. Suddenly, the cat started to vanish! Lily was very surprised and didn't know what to do. She looked around and saw a boy named Tim who was watching her.

"Wow! Did you see that, Tim?" Lily asked. "The cat just vanished!" Tim nodded and said, "Yes, I saw it too. But don't worry, it's a magic cat. It likes to play tricks on people. If we are kind and share our toys, the cat will come back."

Lily and Tim decided to play together and share their toys. After a while, the cat came back and didn't vanish again. They all played happily together. The moral of the story is that when we are kind and share with others, good things will happen.

Sara loves her pet cat, Lily. Lily is soft and warm and likes to play with Sara. Sara hugs Lily and gives her milk and fish. Lily purrs and rubs her head on Sara.

One day, Sara's mom tells her that they have to move to a new house. Sara is sad and scared. She does not want to leave her old house and her friends. She asks her mom, "Can Lily come with us?"

Her mom shakes her head and says, "No, Sara. We are moving to a very cold place. Lily will not like it there. She will be unhappy and sick. We have to send Lily to your aunt's house. She has a big farm and many other cats. Lily will be happy there."

Sara cries and says, "But I will miss Lily. She is my best friend. I don't want to send her away."

Her mom hugs her and says, "I know, Sara. I will miss her too. But we have to do what is best for Lily. She will be safe and warm at your aunt's house. And we can visit her sometimes. And maybe we can get a new pet at our new house. A pet that likes the cold. Like a dog or a rabbit."

Sara wipes her tears and nods. She says, "Okay, mom. I love Lily. I want her to be happy. Can I say goodbye to her?"

Her mom smiles and says, "Of course, Sara. You can say goodbye to her. And you can give her a picture of you and a toy to remember you by."

One day, he went for a walk with his mom and saw a girl in a wheelchair. She had a book in her lap, but she could not turn the pages. She looked sad and lonely. Tom felt sorry for her, but he did not want to talk to her. He thought she was not as gifted as him and he had nothing to learn from her.

His mom saw the girl and smiled. She asked Tom if he wanted to say hello and help her with the book. Tom said no and walked away. He learned that being gifted is not only about what you can do, but also about what you can give.

Before she went to nap, Lily asked her mommy if they could make cookies when they woke up. Her mommy said they could, but only if Lily took a good nap and rested well. 

Lily closed her eyes and fell asleep, dreaming of the delicious cookies she would help her mommy bake when they woke up. When she woke up, she felt refreshed and ready to help her mommy make the best cookies ever. And that's exactly what they did!

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who lived in a big tree. The owl liked to judge the animals in the forest. One day, a little rabbit came to the owl and asked for help. "Can you help me load my basket with carrots?" asked the rabbit. "Of course," said the wise owl. "I will help you load your basket."

As they walked through the forest, the owl noticed that the rabbit was very kind and always helped the other animals. "You are a very kind rabbit," said the wise owl. "Thank you," said the rabbit. "I try to be kind to everyone." 

After they finished loading the basket, the rabbit thanked the owl for his help. "You are a good friend," said the rabbit. "I am happy to help you," said the wise owl. And from that day on, the rabbit and the owl were the best of friends.

The other animals saw the bird and tried to help, but they couldn't untie the knot either. Just when they thought the bird would be stuck forever, a wise old owl came to the rescue. The owl carefully untied the knot and the bird was free!

The bird was so happy that it flew around the tree, singing and chirping with joy. The other animals were happy too, and they all played together in the tree until the end of the day. From that day on, the animals knew they could count on the wise old owl to help them when they needed it.

Lila and Sam were playing outside in the park. They saw a big rainbow in the sky. It had many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.

"Wow, look at the rainbow!" Lila said. "It is so pretty!"

"I want to touch it!" Sam said. "Can we touch it?"

Lila shook her head. "No, we can't touch it. It is too far away. And it is not a thing. It is just light."

Sam frowned. He wanted to touch the rainbow. He wondered how it would feel. He thought it would be soft and warm.

He saw a big puddle on the ground. It had some of the rainbow colors in it. He ran to the puddle and put his hand in it.

"Sam, what are you doing?" Lila asked. "You are getting wet!"

"I am touching the rainbow!" Sam said. "Look, it is in the water!"

Lila ran to him and looked at the puddle. She saw the colors too. But they were not the same as the rainbow. They were blurry and mixed. And they moved when Sam touched them.

"That is not the rainbow, Sam. That is something else. Something unknown." Lila said.

"What is unknown?" Sam asked.

"Unknown is something you don't know. Something new. Something different." Lila said.

"Is unknown good or bad?" Sam asked.

Lila shrugged. "I don't know. Maybe both. Maybe neither. Maybe it depends."

Sam nodded. He liked unknown. He liked new and different. He liked to touch and learn.

He smiled and said, "Let's find more unknown things!"

Lila smiled too and said, "OK, let's go!"

They held hands and ran to explore the park. They looked for more unknown things to touch and see. They had fun and learned a lot. They forgot about the rainbow in the sky. But they made their own rainbow in their minds.

"I told you to be careful, Sara!" Tom said. He felt sorry for Sara and hugged her. "Do you want a band-aid?"

"Yes, please," Sara said. She sniffed and wiped her tears. "That was a mean lizard."

Tom and Sara went inside the house. Mom saw Sara's hand and gave her a band-aid. She also gave them some cookies and milk. Sara put the band-aid on her hand and ate a cookie. She felt better.

"Next time, let's look for something else, OK?" Tom said.

"OK," Sara said. She smiled at Tom. "How about a white bunny?"

One day, they met a new boy in the park. His name was Max, and he had a big blue bike. He saw Tom and Lily's top and said, "That's a silly toy. It's too slow and boring. My bike is much better. It can go very fast and make loud noises. Do you want to see?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They were curious about Max's bike. They followed him to a hill, where he got on his bike and said, "Watch this!" He pushed the start button, and the bike made a loud roar. He zoomed down the hill, leaving a trail of smoke behind him.

Tom and Lily were amazed. They had never seen a bike like that. They clapped and cheered. "Wow, that's so cool!" they said.

Max came back, looking very proud. He said, "See? I told you my bike is better. Your top is just a lazy toy. It can't do anything. Why don't you give it to me, and I'll let you ride my bike?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They liked their top. It was their favorite toy. They didn't want to give it to Max. But they also wanted to try his bike. It looked like fun. They didn't know what to do.

Then, they had an idea. They said, "OK, Max. We'll give you our top, but only if you can make it spin faster than your bike. Can you do that?"

Max laughed. He said, "Of course I can. That's easy. Give me your top, and I'll show you."

Tom and Lily gave him their top. Max took it and said, "Watch this!" He threw the top on the ground, and kicked it hard. He expected it to spin very fast, and then stop.

Tom and Lily gasped. They saw their top broken and sad. They felt angry and sad too. They said, "Max, you broke our top! That's not nice! You're a mean boy!"

Max looked surprised. He said, "Oops. Sorry. I didn't mean to. It was an accident. Here, take your top back. I don't want it anyway. It's a silly toy."

But Tom and Lily didn't want their top back. It was too late. It was ruined. They said, "No, thank you. You can keep it. We don't want to play with you anymore. You're a bad boy!"

They turned around and ran away. They left Max alone with his bike and their broken top. He felt sorry and sad too. He wished he had been nicer to Tom and Lily. The bee and the caterpillar watched until the ambulance was far away and then the bee said, "Let's go home now, caterpillar. That was an exciting spin!" 

The caterpillar agreed and the bee flew him back down to the ground. From then on, the caterpillar loved to go for spins and he could never forget the exciting time he had when the ambulance drove by.

Tim and Lily caught the rat and put it in the box. They were very happy and proud. They did not see that the rat had sharp teeth and claws. They did not see that the rat was angry and hungry. They did not see that the box had holes.

They took the box to their room and put it on their bed. They wanted to show their mom their new pet. They left the box for a moment and went to find their mom. They did not close the door.

The rat saw its chance and escaped from the box. It was very mad and wanted to hurt Tim and Lily. It jumped on their bed and tore their toys and sheets. It scratched their pillows and books. It made a big mess and a loud noise.

Tim and Lily came back with their mom and saw the rat on their bed. They were very shocked and scared. They screamed and ran away. Their mom was very angry and sad. She told them that they were naughty and careless. She told them that they had to clean their room and throw away the rat. She told them that they had no pet and no toys. She told them that they had to behave, or else.

Sara was playing with her doll in the garden. She liked to dress her doll in a pretty skirt and a hat. She was happy and sang a song.

But then a big dog came and ran towards her. The dog barked loud and jumped on her. Sara was scared and dropped her doll. The dog grabbed the doll by the skirt and ran away.

Sara wept and wept. She wanted her doll back. She felt hurt and sad. She cried for her mom.

Her mom heard her and came to the garden. She saw Sara crying and hugged her.

"What happened, my sweetie?" she asked.

"A big dog took my doll!" Sara sobbed. "He tore her skirt and ran away!"

"Oh, I'm sorry, Sara. That was a bad dog. He should not do that. Come, let's go and look for your doll. Maybe we can find her and fix her skirt."

Sara nodded and wiped her tears. She held her mom's hand and walked with her. She hoped they could find her doll and make her pretty again. She loved her doll very much.

Lani and Kato were two friends who liked to play in the forest. They had a game where they pretended to be hunters and chased animals with sticks. They called their sticks spears.

One day, they saw a big black bird sitting on a branch. They wanted to catch it and make it their pet. They crept closer and closer, holding their spears. Lani was in front, and Kato was behind.

When they were very close, Lani threw his spear at the bird. But he missed, and the spear flew past the bird and hit Kato in the arm. Kato cried out in pain and dropped his spear. The bird flew away, scared by the noise.

Lani ran to Kato and said he was sorry. He helped him get up and took him to his mom. She put a bandage on his wound and gave him a hug. She told Lani and Kato that they should not play with spears, because they could hurt themselves or others. She said they should use their words, not their weapons, to make friends with animals.

Lani and Kato learned their lesson. They said they were sorry to each other and to the bird. They decided to play a different game, where they pretended to be explorers and looked for flowers and bugs. They had more fun and did not get hurt. They were happy and kind.

Ben likes to write poems. He writes them on paper with his crayons. He writes about his toys, his dog, his mom and dad. He thinks poems are fun and pretty.

One day, he finds a big book on the shelf. It has many poems inside. He wants to read them, but the words are too hard. He asks his mom to read them to him, but she is busy. He asks his dad, but he is on the phone. He feels sad and bored.

He has an idea. He takes his crayons and writes on the book. He writes his own poems over the old ones. He writes about his fish, his bike, his cake. He thinks he is making the book better.

But then, his mom comes and sees what he has done. She is very angry. She says, "Ben, what have you done? You have ruined the book! This is not your book, this is grandma's book! She gave it to me when I was little. It is very special and old. You cannot write on it!"

Ben feels guilty. He did not know the book was grandma's. He did not know it was special and old. He says, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to write poems. I like poems. I did not mean to ruin the book."

His mom sighs. She is still angry, but she loves Ben. She says, "I know you like poems, Ben. But you cannot write on other people's things. You have to ask first. And you have to be careful with old things. They can break easily. Do you understand?"

Ben nods. He understands. He says, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you. I love grandma. Can we fix the book?"

His mom hugs him. She says, "I love you too, Ben. I love grandma too. We can try to fix the book. But first, you have to say sorry to grandma. And you have to write her a poem. A nice poem. On a new paper. Can you do that?"

Ben smiles. He says, "Yes, mom. I can do that. I can write a nice poem for grandma. I hope she likes it."

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big tree with purple flowers. Anna likes the tree. She wants to pick a flower.

"Can I have a flower, Ben?" she asks.

"No, Anna. You can't," Ben says. "The tree is not ours. We have to be nice to the tree."

"But I want a flower. It is so pretty," Anna says. She tries to reach the flower.

"Stop, Anna. You will hurt the tree," Ben says. He pulls her hand.

Anna is angry. She does not listen to Ben. She insists on getting a flower. She pulls harder.

"Ouch!" Anna cries. A bee stings her finger. The bee was hiding in the flower.

Anna drops the flower. She runs to Ben. She is crying.

"I'm sorry, Ben. You were right. I was wrong," she says.

Ben hugs her. He is kind. He says, "It's okay, Anna. I forgive you. Let's go find some ice for your finger."

They leave the tree alone. The tree is happy. The bee is happy. Anna and Ben are happy. They learned a lesson.

Lisa and Ben are friends. They like to play and laugh together. Today is Lisa's birthday. She is very happy. She invites Ben to her party.

At the party, there are many balloons, cakes, and toys. Lisa and Ben have fun with the other kids. They play games, sing songs, and eat yummy food. Lisa's mom gives her a big present. It is a teddy bear. Lisa loves teddy bears. She hugs it and says thank you.

Ben thinks of a joke. He wants to make Lisa laugh. He takes a balloon and pops it behind Lisa's ear. He says, "Boo!" Lisa is scared. She drops her teddy bear. The teddy bear falls on the floor. A dog runs and grabs it. The dog bites the teddy bear and tears it apart.

Lisa cries. She is very sad. She says, "Ben, you are mean! You ruined my birthday! You are not my friend anymore!" Ben feels sorry. He says, "Lisa, I'm sorry. I was only joking. I didn't mean to scare you. Please forgive me." But Lisa does not listen. She runs to her mom and hugs her. She does not want to talk to Ben.

The party is over. Lisa and Ben do not celebrate anymore. They do not play and laugh together. They are both unhappy. The teddy bear was adorable, but now it is gone. The joke was not funny, but now it is too late. The end.

Tim and Sam like to play ball in the park. They throw the ball to each other and catch it. They have fun and laugh.

One day, they see a big fence near the park. The fence has a sign that says "Keep Out". Tim and Sam are curious. They want to see what is behind the fence.

They climb over the fence and find a big field. The field has many flowers and trees. They also see a big machine. The machine is loud and dirty. It digs holes in the ground.

"Wow, look at that!" Tim says. "Let's go closer and touch it!"

"No, Tim, that's not a good idea," Sam says. "The sign says keep out. The machine might be dangerous. Let's go back."

But Tim does not listen. He is careless. He runs to the machine and tries to climb on it. He does not see the man who drives the machine. The man does not see Tim either. He is busy and tired.

The man moves the machine. The machine has a big arm that swings in the air. The arm hits Tim hard. Tim falls to the ground. He does not get up.

Sam screams. He runs to Tim and shakes him. He cries and calls for help. But no one hears him. The fence is too high and the machine is too loud.

The end.

Sara and Ben were playing by the river. They saw a big raft made of wood and rope. It looked new and fun.

"Can we go on the raft?" Sara asked Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe it belongs to someone," Ben said.

They looked around, but they did not see anyone. The raft was tied to a tree with a long rope.

"Let's try it. Just for a little bit," Sara said. She untied the rope and climbed on the raft. Ben followed her.

The raft started to move with the water. It was fast and bumpy. Sara and Ben laughed and held on.

"Look, there's a duck!" Sara pointed to a brown duck swimming near them.

"Quack, quack!" Ben said, trying to sound like the duck.

The duck looked at them and quacked back. Sara and Ben smiled.

They did not see the big rock ahead. The raft hit the rock and tipped over. Sara and Ben fell into the water. They were wet and scared.

"Help, help!" they shouted.

A man heard them and ran to the river. He had a fishing rod and a hat. He was the owner of the raft.

"What are you doing on my raft?" he asked, pulling them out of the water.

"We're sorry, mister. We just wanted to play," Sara said.

"Well, you should have asked first. And you should be careful. The river is dangerous," the man said.

He gave them a towel and took them to their parents. Sara and Ben said sorry again and thanked him.

They learned their lesson. They never went on the raft again. They played with their own toys instead.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They also liked to look at the sky and see the birds and clouds. Sometimes they saw a jet, a big and fast thing that made a loud noise.

"Look, Mia, a jet!" Sam said, pointing up. "It is so high and shiny. I want to fly in a jet one day."

"Me too, Sam. Maybe we can go to a place with many jets and pick one to ride. That would be fun," Mia said.

They kept playing and dreaming about jets. They did not see the man who was watching them from a bench. He had a big bag and a hat. He looked angry and mean. He wanted to take Sam and Mia away and make them work for him. He had a plan.

He waited until Sam and Mia were near the slide. Then he walked over and said, "Hello, kids. Do you like jets? I have a jet in my bag. Do you want to see it?"

Sam and Mia were curious. They liked jets. They did not know the man was bad. They said, "Yes, please. Can we see your jet?"

The man smiled, but not a nice smile. He opened his bag and showed them a toy jet. It was small and plastic. It did not look like a real jet. It looked cheap and broken.

"Wow, a jet!" Sam said, but he was disappointed. He wanted to see a real jet, not a toy jet.

"Can we play with it?" Mia asked, trying to be polite.

"Sure, sure. But you have to come with me first. I have more jets in my car. You can pick any one you like. Come on, let's go," the man said, grabbing their hands.

Sam and Mia felt scared. They did not want to go with the man. They did not know him. They wanted to stay in the park. They wanted to see their mom and dad.

"Help! Help!" they shouted, trying to pull away.

The man tried to drag them to his car. He was strong and mean. He did not care about Sam and Mia. He only wanted to use them.

But then, something happened. A real jet flew over the park. It was big and fast and loud. It was graceful and shiny. It made a beautiful trail in the sky. It was a jet that Sam and Mia had never seen before. It was a jet that the man had never seen before. It was a jet that belonged to the police.

The police jet saw the man and the kids. It saw that the man was bad and the kids were in trouble. It flew down and made a loud noise. It scared the man and made him let go of Sam and Mia. It called for help and told the other police where to find the man and the kids.

Sam and Mia ran away from the man. They ran to the slide, where they saw their mom and dad. They hugged them and told them what happened. They were safe and happy.

The police came and caught the man. They took him away and put him in jail. They thanked the jet for saving the kids. They gave Sam and Mia a badge and a sticker. They said they were brave and smart.

Sam and Mia smiled. They thanked the police and the jet. They said they liked jets, but only the good ones. They said they would never go with a stranger again. They said they would always stay with their mom and dad.

They went back to playing in the park. They looked at the sky and saw the jet fly away. It was graceful and shiny. It made a beautiful trail in the sky. It was a jet that Sam and Mia would always remember.

Tom and Lily were twins. They liked to play and have fun. One day, their mom made a big cake for their birthday. It had pink frosting and sprinkles. It looked yummy.

Mom said, "The cake is still hot. You have to wait until it cools down. Then we can cut it and eat it. Be good and don't touch it."

Tom and Lily nodded. They went to their room and played with their toys. But soon they got bored. They wanted to see the cake.

They tiptoed to the kitchen. They saw the cake on the table. It smelled good. They wanted a taste.

Lily said, "Let's take a little bit. Mom won't notice."

Tom said, "OK. But be careful. Don't make a mess."

Lily reached for the cake. She tried to balance on a chair. But the chair was wobbly. She slipped and fell. She knocked over the cake. It landed on the floor. It was a big mess.

Tom and Lily gasped. They heard Mom coming. They were scared. They ran to hide.

Mom saw the cake on the floor. She was angry. She said, "Who did this? Who ruined the cake?"

Tom and Lily came out of their hiding place. They looked sad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We wanted a taste. We didn't mean to."

Mom sighed. She said, "I know you were curious. But you should have listened to me. The cake was hot and fragile. You could have burned yourself or hurt yourself. And now we have no cake for your birthday."

Tom and Lily felt bad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We love you. Can we help you clean up?"

Mom smiled. She said, "I love you too. Yes, you can help me clean up. And don't worry. We can still have a happy birthday. I have another cake in the freezer. It's not as big or as pretty, but it's still tasty. And it's not hot or wobbly. We can have it after dinner. How does that sound?"

Tom and Lily cheered. They said, "That sounds great, Mom. Thank you. You're the best."

They hugged Mom and helped her clean up. They learned their lesson. They never touched the cake again until Mom said so. They had a happy birthday after all.

He came out of the cave and looked for Lila. He saw her sitting on a bench, crying. He felt sorry for her. He walked to her and said, "I'm sorry I was mad at you. I know you were scared of the spider. Do you want to play with me again?"

Lila looked up and saw Tom. She smiled and said, "I'm sorry I ran away. I know you wanted to see the cave. Do you want to play with me again?"

"Look, Jen, a box! Maybe it has a surprise for us!" Tim says.

He tries to open the box, but it is locked. He looks for a key, but he cannot find one.

"Maybe we can unlock it with something else," Jen says. She sees a string on the floor. She picks it up and gives it to Tim.

"Good idea, Jen! Let's try it!" Tim says.

He puts the string in the lock and pulls it hard. The lock does not open. He pulls harder and harder. The string breaks and the lock stays closed.

"Oh no, the string is broken!" Tim says. He feels ashamed. He thinks he ruined the string.

"I'm sorry, Jen. I broke your string. It was a bad idea," he says.

Jen hugs Tim and smiles.

"It's okay, Tim. It was not my string. It was your mom's string. She uses it to sew clothes. Maybe we can ask her to fix it," she says.

"Really? It was not your string?" Tim says.

"No, it was not. And it was not a bad idea. It was a smart idea. You tried to unlock the box. Maybe next time we can find a key," Jen says.

Tim feels better. He hugs Jen back and smiles.

"Thank you, Jen. You are a good friend. Maybe we can play with something else. Do you want to play with my cars?" he says.

"Yes, I do. I like your cars. They are fast and fun," Jen says.

They forget about the box and play with the cars. They are happy.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they go to church with their moms. They see many people in the church. Some people are happy, some people are sad.

"Why are some people sad?" Jen asks Tom.

"Maybe they have no toys or books," Tom says.

"That is sad," Jen says. "We have many toys and books. We are lucky."

"Yes, we are," Tom says. "Maybe we can give some of our toys and books to the sad people. Then they will be happy too."

"That is a good idea," Jen says. "Let's do that."

Tom and Jen go home and find some toys and books they do not play with anymore. They put them in a big bag. They go back to the church with their moms. They see the sad people again. They give them the toys and books from the bag.

"Here, this is for you," Tom and Jen say. "We hope you like them."

The sad people smile and say thank you. They hug Tom and Jen. They look happy now.

Tom and Jen feel happy too. They have done a good thing. They have shared their toys and books with the sad people. They have made them happy.

The moral of the story is: It is good to share what you have with others who have less. Sharing makes everyone happy.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys and books. One day, they find a big box in the living room. It has a sticker that says "mail". They are curious and want to open it.

"Can we see what is inside?" Ben asks his mom.

"No, not yet. This is a special mail for your dad. He will open it when he comes home from work. It is a surprise for his birthday." Mom says.

"But we want to see it too!" Sam says.

"Sorry, you have to wait. Why don't you play with your other toys?" Mom says.

Ben and Sam are not happy. They want to know what is in the box. They think it is something fun and cool. They sneak to the box when mom is not looking. They try to open it, but it is taped and hard to open. They look for something to cut the tape. They find a pair of scissors on the table.

"Be careful with those!" Mom says. "They are sharp and can hurt you. Put them back!"

But Ben and Sam do not listen. They take the scissors and cut the tape. They open the box and see what is inside. It is a big book with a black cover and a silver star. It has a lot of words and pictures. They think it is a magic book.

"Wow, look at this!" Ben says.

"Maybe it has spells!" Sam says.

They open the book and see a page that says "Do not read this aloud". They do not know what "aloud" means. They think it means "loud". They want to try a spell. They see a spell that says "Make something dead". They do not know what "dead" means. They think it means "sleep". They want to make something sleep. They see their cat, Fluffy, sleeping on the couch. They point at Fluffy and read the spell aloud.

"Make something dead! Make something dead! Make something dead!" They chant.

Suddenly, Fluffy stops breathing. He does not move. He does not wake up. He is dead.

Ben and Sam are scared. They do not know what they did. They close the book and put it back in the box. They run to their mom and cry.

"Mom, mom, something bad happened!" Ben says.

"What is it? What did you do?" Mom asks.

"We opened the mail and read the book and said the spell and Fluffy is dead!" Sam says.

Ben and Sam are sorry. They did not mean to do this. They did not know what they did. They hug mom and say they are sorry. They cry and say they miss Fluffy.

Mom hugs them and says she is sorry too. She says she loves them, but they have to learn to listen and obey. She says they have to say sorry to dad too. She says they have to bury Fluffy and say goodbye. She says they have to be careful with words and books and spells. She says they have to be good boys and not do this again.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Anna had a cute doll that she loved very much. Ben had a big truck that he liked to zoom around. They were having fun, but they also wanted to try something new.

"Let's make a wish," Anna said. "Maybe it will come true."

"OK," Ben said. "What do you wish for?"

"I wish I could shrink and be as small as my doll," Anna said. "Then I could play with her in her house and dress her up."

"I wish I could shrink and be as small as my truck," Ben said. "Then I could drive it around and go on adventures."

They closed their eyes and wished very hard. Suddenly, they felt a strange tingling in their bodies. They opened their eyes and gasped. They had shrunk! They were as small as their toys!

"Wow!" Anna said. "Our wish came true!"

"Awesome!" Ben said. "Let's go play!"

They ran to their toys and climbed on them. Anna went inside the doll's house and found many clothes and accessories for her and her doll. Ben drove the truck around the living room and pretended to be a firefighter, a racer, and a explorer. They had a lot of fun, but they also missed their mom and dad.

"Ben," Anna said after a while. "Do you think we can go back to our normal size?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe we have to wish again."

"OK," Anna said. "Let's do it."

They closed their eyes and wished very hard. They wished to be big again. They felt another tingling in their bodies. They opened their eyes and smiled. They had grown back! They were as big as before!

"Yay!" Anna said. "We are big again!"

"Hooray!" Ben said. "That was cool!"

They hugged their toys and put them away. They ran to their mom and dad and told them about their adventure. Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them.

"That sounds like a wonderful wish," their mom said.

"But we are happy to be with you," their dad said.

"We love you," Anna and Ben said.

The end.

Anna liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors, but her favorite was red. She used red to draw flowers, hearts, and her name. She was very proud of her drawings and wanted to show them to her mom.

But mom was busy in the kitchen. She was making a cake for Anna's birthday. She told Anna to wait until she was done. Anna waited, but she was bored. She looked around the living room and saw a big book on the shelf. It had a picture of a castle on the cover. Anna wondered what was inside.

She climbed on a chair and reached for the book. But the book was heavy and old. When Anna pulled it, it made a loud noise and fell on the floor. The book opened and a cloud of dust came out. Anna coughed and sneezed. She saw the pages of the book. They had words and pictures, but they were not like her drawings. They were faded and torn. Anna did not like the book. She wanted her crayons.

She looked for her crayons, but they were not on the table. They were on the floor, under the book. Anna tried to lift the book, but it was too heavy. She could not see her crayons. She felt sad and angry. She wanted her crayons back. She wanted to draw.

She shouted, "Mom, mom, help me! The book took my crayons!"

Mom heard Anna's shout and ran to the living room. She saw the book, the dust, and the crayons. She was surprised and worried. She asked Anna what happened. Anna told her the story. Mom hugged Anna and said, "I'm sorry, honey. The book did not mean to take your crayons. It is a very old and original book. It has stories and pictures from a long time ago. It is very special and rare. But it is also very fragile and delicate. We have to be careful with it."

Mom lifted the book and put it back on the shelf. She wiped the dust from the floor and the table. She gave Anna her crayons and said, "Here you go, sweetie. You can draw again. But please, don't touch the book again. It is not a toy. It is a treasure."

Anna nodded and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry. I won't touch the book again. But can I see the pictures?"

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a secret spot under a big tree, where they hid their toys and snacks.

One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He was bigger and louder than them. He ran around and kicked the ball and the swing. He made a lot of noise and scared the birds and the squirrels.

"Who is he?" Lily asked Ben.

"I don't know. He looks mean," Ben said.

They watched him from their secret spot. They hoped he would not find them.

But he did. He saw their toys and snacks under the tree. He ran over and grabbed them. He laughed and threw them around.

"Hey, those are ours!" Lily shouted.

"Give them back!" Ben said.

They ran out of their secret spot and tried to get their things. But the new boy was too strong and fast. He pushed them away and made fun of them.

"Go away, you babies! These are mine now!" he said.

Lily and Ben were very upset. They felt sad and angry. They wanted their toys and snacks back. They wanted the new boy to leave.

They did not know what to do.

But then, they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you! What are you doing?" the voice said.

It was the park ranger. He had seen everything. He was not happy.

He walked over to the new boy and took the toys and snacks from him. He gave them back to Lily and Ben.

"Are you okay, kids?" he asked.

"Yes, thank you," Lily and Ben said.

They smiled and hugged their toys and snacks.

The park ranger looked at the new boy. He frowned and shook his head.

"You should not take things that are not yours. You should not push and hurt other kids. You should not be rude and noisy. You should be nice and polite. Do you understand?" he said.

The new boy nodded. He looked scared and sorry.

"I'm sorry," he said.

He turned to Lily and Ben.

"I'm sorry, too. Can we be friends?" he asked.

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They thought for a moment.

They decided to give him a chance.

"Okay, we can be friends. But you have to be nice and share," Lily said.

"And you have to be quiet and gentle," Ben said.

The new boy agreed. He smiled and said his name was Sam.

They all went to their secret spot under the tree. They played with their toys and shared their snacks. They talked and laughed and had fun.

They became friends.

"Let's roll the bus on the floor," Sara says. "We can pretend we are going to the park."

"Okay," Tom says. "I will be the driver and you will be the passenger."

They roll the bus on the floor. They make noises like the bus is honking and moving. They have fun.

But then Tom sees a bump on the floor. It is a book that Mom left there. Tom thinks it will be fun to roll the bus over the bump.

"Watch this, Sara," Tom says. "The bus will go up and down."

He rolls the bus faster and faster. He aims for the bump. The bus hits the bump and flies in the air. It lands on the couch.

"Hey, Rex, stop!" Ben shouted. He was angry. He did not want Rex to ruin their zoom. He kicked Rex in the nose. Rex yelped and ran away.

Mia was scared. She did not like Rex. She did not like Ben's kick. She started to cry. "Ben, you are mean! You hurt Rex! You hurt me!" She got out of the box and ran to her room.

Ben felt bad. He did not mean to hurt Rex or Mia. He loved them. He got out of the box and followed Mia. He knocked on her door. "Mia, I'm sorry. I was just trying to save our zoom. Can we be friends again?"

Mia opened the door. She saw Ben's face. He looked sad. She felt sorry for him. She hugged him. "It's okay, Ben. I'm sorry too. I know you love our zoom. Can we fix it?"

Ben nodded. He hugged her back. "Yes, we can fix it. And we can play with Rex too. He is a good dog. He just wanted to have fun."

They went back to the living room. They found some tape and glued the box back together. They also gave Rex a treat and a pat. They all got inside the box and pretended to drive again. They had fun. They were happy. They were friends.

His friends loved the game! They laughed and played as they searched for the numbers. Soon, they forgot about the cold outside. Tim was not sad anymore. He was happy that he could have fun with his friends, even on a cold day.

One day, a player named Tim went to the park to play. He loved to jump and play with his friends. Tim saw his friend, Sam, and went to say "hi."

As they played, a rude boy came to the park. He pushed Tim while he was jumping. Tim fell down and felt sad. Sam said to the rude boy, "You should not push. It's not nice to be rude."

The rude boy thought about it and said, "I'm sorry. I will be nice now." So, Tim, Sam, and the rude boy played together and had fun. They all learned that being nice is better than being rude.

One day, a little girl named Amy was playing outside. It was a cold day, and everything was starting to freeze. Amy felt her hands getting very cold, so she went inside her house to find her mom.

"Mom, my hands are cold and dry," said Amy. Her mom looked at her and said, "You need some lotion, dear." She gave Amy a bottle of lotion to put on her hands. Amy felt better after using the lotion, and her hands were not dry anymore.

Amy wanted to go back outside, but she did not want to be foolish again. She asked her mom, "Can I have gloves too?" Her mom smiled and gave her gloves to keep her hands warm. Now, Amy could play outside without feeling cold. She learned to always wear gloves on cold days, so her hands would not freeze and need lotion again.

The bird was so happy that Fluffy and Lily helped it. From that day on, Fluffy, Lily, and the bird became the best of friends, and they all played catch together.
