Then her mom showed her a magazine. She said it was special and delicate. Sarah opened the magazine and saw pretty pictures and happy stories.

The magazine helped Sarah to feel better. She looked at the pictures and smiled again. The comforting hug, the delicate magazine and her real friends made Sarah feel happy and loved.

Once upon a time there was a little 3 year old boy called Ben. Ben was a very polite boy, he always said please and thank you! 

One day, Ben was playing outside when he saw something strange. It was a hook hanging from a tree. Ben wanted to see what it was so he walked towards it but suddenly he heard a loud voice. 

"Stop! Freeze!" said the voice. 

Ben froze immediately. He looked around and saw a big bear standing a few metres away from him. He was scared!

The bear said "This is my playground, I don't want you to touch the hook".

But Ben was polite, so he said "I'm sorry, I won't touch it. I was just curious".

The bear replied "That's okay, just be careful and don't touch the hook". 

Ben nodded and said "I won't, I promise. Thank you". 

The bear smiled and said "You are very polite, now go and have fun!" 

Ben smiled with relief and ran off to play. From then on, he remembered to always respect the things that belong to others.

Sadie started to do her act, but then something happened and she made a mistake. She was embarrassed and instantly put her head down. Suddenly, her mom came up to her with a big hug and said, "It's ok, Sadie. Everyone makes mistakes!".

Sadie was still a bit ashamed of her mistake, but she decided to perform the act again. This time, she completed it wonderfully and everyone cheered! Sadie was very proud of herself and her mom gave her an even bigger hug. From then on, Sadie never felt ashamed of her mistakes, and she always performed her best.

Once there was a strong horse named Daisy. Daisy lived in a stable and everyday she worked hard, pulling a heavy carriage. One day, Daisy's tired legs gave way and she could no longer pull the carriage. 

The carriage driver was angry and ran over to the stable to find Daisy. He shouted at Daisy, saying "You can't do your job any more!" 

Daisy looked up at him with her big brown eyes. She said "I just need rest - then I can be strong again". The carriage driver thought about this and realised that Daisy was right. He said with a kinder voice "OK, I will give you the rest you need".

And so the driver gave Daisy a long rest and when she was strong again, Daisy was once again able to pull the carriage. The moral of the story is: if you work too hard and get tired, it's OK to ask for a rest so you can be strong again.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who was very hungry. He asked his mum, "Can I have some food?"

Mum said, "Yes, but hurry! We only have a potato and you need to eat it quickly!"

The little boy kept saying, "Hurry, hurry" as he ran to the kitchen. He grabbed the potato and put it in the oven. 

While the potato was cooking, the little boy began to feel a bit bored. So he decided to go outside and look for something to do.

Unfortunately, the little boy didn't see the big, sharp rock. He stepped on it, and it hurt his foot. He cried out in pain, "Ouch! It hurt!"

Just then his mum came outside and saw what had happened. She picked him up and held him close. "It's okay, darling," she said, "Let's go back inside and get you some food. Now hurry!"

They quickly went back inside and took the potato out of the oven. The little boy bit into it and it was delicious! 

He smiled as he ate and soon he was feeling much better. "That was tasty," he said. 

His mum smiled too. "See," she said, "sometimes it pays to hurry!" 

The little boy nodded and smiled. He was very happy and full now.

John knew he had made a mistake. He picked up the glass to make it better. He wiped the floor with a cloth to make it clean again.

John nodded and agreed. He never wanted to make his mommy angry like that again!

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who was very sad. He carried a big sack and walked very slowly. Everywhere he went, he made people weep.

The sack he carried was so heavy that it made his back hurt. People from far and wide would come to see him and ask why he was so sad.

He would touch his sack and shake his head sadly. Then he would start to weep. He would tell them that his life was so hard, and how he was so tired from carrying his sack.

The people in the village would quietly slip away, but no one knew how to make him feel better. So they all wept, because the elderly man seemed so very sad.

Tim and Kim were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They shared their toys and snacks. They were dependable friends.

One day, a big dog came to the park. It was black and brown and had sharp teeth. It barked and ran towards Tim and Kim. They were scared and ran away. But the dog was faster and caught Tim by his leg. It bit him hard and made him bleed. Kim screamed and hoped someone would help.

A man heard Kim and came to the park. He saw the dog and Tim. He shouted at the dog and threw a stick. The dog let go of Tim and ran away. The man picked up Tim and carried him to his car. He said he would take him to the hospital. Kim followed him and cried.

At the hospital, the doctor looked at Tim's leg. He said it was a bad bite and he had to give him a shot. He said the shot would stop the germs from making him sick. He said the dog might have had rabies. He said Tim had to stay in the hospital for a few days. Kim said she was sorry and hugged Tim. Tim said it was not her fault and thanked her for being his friend.

The next day, Kim came to visit Tim. She brought him a balloon and a card. She said she missed him and hoped he would get better soon. But Tim looked pale and weak. He said he felt very bad and his skin was hot. He said the shot did not work and he had rabies. He said he was going to die. Kim was shocked and sad. She did not know what to say. She held his hand and cried.

The moral of the story is: Be careful of strange dogs. They can be dangerous and hurt you. If a dog bites you, you should tell an adult and go to the hospital right away. You should also get a vaccine to prevent rabies. Rabies is a very serious disease that can kill you. You should love and cherish your friends. They can help you and comfort you when you are in trouble.

She saw a big mirror on the wall. She ran to it and looked at herself. She saw her red lips and her brown eyes. She thought she looked pretty. She wanted to see more of herself. She moved closer to the mirror. She saw her nose and her ears. She moved even closer. She saw her eyelashes and her freckles. She moved so close that her nose touched the mirror. She saw her nose make a mark on the glass. She giggled.

She moved back a little and saw her whole face again. She noticed something. Her lips looked thin. She wanted them to look bigger. She thought of a way. She took the red stick again and rubbed it more on her lips. She rubbed it all over her mouth. She felt the red thing spread more and more. She smiled and looked at the mirror again.

She saw her mouth and gasped. It was not pretty. It was red and messy. It looked like she ate a lot of berries and spilled them on her face. She did not like it. She wanted to take it off. She rubbed her mouth with her hand. She saw the red thing spread on her hand. She rubbed her hand on her shirt. She saw the red thing spread on her shirt. She started to cry.

She heard her mom come in. She saw her mom look at her and the mirror and the red stick. She saw her mom's eyes get big and her mouth open. She heard her mom say, "Oh, Sara, what did you do?" She nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I just wanted to look pretty like you." She heard her mom say, "You are pretty, Sara, with or without makeup. You are my beautiful girl." She smiled and hugged her mom back. She felt happy.

Tom and Mia live in a big city with many tall buildings and cars. They like to play with their toys and watch TV, but sometimes they miss nature. They miss the green trees, the blue sky, the colorful flowers and the animals.

One day, their mom says, "We are going to visit grandma and grandpa in the countryside. They have a farm with cows, chickens, pigs and a dog. You can help them feed the animals and play outside."

Tom and Mia are very happy and excited. They pack their bags and get in the car. They drive for a long time and see the city change into fields and hills.

When they arrive at the farm, they hug grandma and grandpa and run to see the animals. They pet the dog, feed the cows, collect the eggs and watch the pigs. They laugh and have fun.

But then, they see a big tractor coming. The tractor is loud and scary. It has a big shovel and it starts to dig the ground. Grandma and grandpa look sad and angry. They say, "The tractor is here to build a new road. The road will go through our farm and destroy our land. We don't want the road. We want to keep our farm and our nature."

Tom and Mia feel sad and angry too. They don't want the tractor to ruin their grandma and grandpa's farm. They don't want the road to take away their nature. They want to stop the tractor.

They run to the tractor and shout, "Stop! Stop! Go away! Leave our farm alone! We love our farm and our nature!"

The tractor driver hears them and stops. He gets out and looks at them. He says, "I'm sorry, kids. I'm just doing my job. The road is part of a modern plan to connect the city and the countryside. The road will make it easier for people to travel and trade. The road will bring more money and opportunities."

Tom and Mia don't understand. They say, "But what about the animals? What about the flowers? What about the trees? What about the farm? What about grandma and grandpa? Don't they matter?"

The tractor driver sighs. He says, "They do matter, kids. But sometimes, progress comes with a price. Sometimes, we have to choose between the old and the new, between the past and the future, between nature and modern. It's not easy, but it's how the world works."

Tom and Mia shake their heads. They say, "We don't like this world. We don't like this choice. We don't like this road. We don't like this tractor. We like our farm. We like our nature. We like our grandma and grandpa. We miss our nature. We miss our farm. We miss our grandma and grandpa."

The tractor driver looks at them with pity. He says, "I'm sorry, kids. I wish I could make you happy. But I can't. I have to do my job. I have to build this road. I have to be modern."

He gets back in the tractor and starts the engine. He says, "Goodbye, kids. Goodbye, farm. Goodbye, nature."

He drives away, leaving behind a trail of dust and tears.

But the tree was not a banana tree. It was a monkey tree. A big monkey was hiding behind the leaves. He did not like the children who wanted to take his food. He jumped out and made a loud noise. "Ooo-ooo-aaa-aaa!" he shouted.

Anna and Ben were frightened. They screamed and ran away. The monkey chased them for a while, then went back to his tree. He ate his bananas and smiled.

Anna and Ben learned a lesson. They should not take things that are not theirs. They should be careful of animals they do not know. They should respect nature and its creatures.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play at the beach. They see a big boat on the water. They want to go on the boat.

"Can we go on the boat, Mom?" Tom asks.

"No, you can't. The boat is for big people. It is too far and too fast for you," Mom says.

Tom and Sam are sad. They think the boat is fun. They see something in the water. It is a big whale. The whale is weak. It has a net around it. The net hurts the whale.

"Look, Sam! A whale!" Tom says.

"Wow! A whale! It is so big!" Sam says.

The whale makes a noise. It sounds like it is asking for help. Tom and Sam want to help the whale. They think the net is bad.

"Can we help the whale, Mom?" Sam asks.

"Yes, you can. But you have to be careful. The whale is big and strong. It can hurt you if it moves," Mom says.

Mom gives Tom and Sam a pair of scissors. They go to the water. They swim to the whale. They cut the net with the scissors. The whale is free. It is happy. It thanks Tom and Sam with a splash.

"Yay! We helped the whale!" Tom says.

"We are good friends!" Sam says.

The whale swims away. It waves with its tail. Tom and Sam wave back. They are happy. They think the whale is nice. They go back to the beach. They hug Mom. They play with the sand. They have a good day.

One day, a hunter went to the forest to find some food. He had a bow and some arrows, and a big bag to carry what he caught. He was very hungry and poor, and he hoped to find a deer or a rabbit.

He walked and walked, but he did not see any animals. He only saw trees and rocks and birds. He was getting tired and sad. He decided to rest under a big tree and eat some bread. He put his bow and arrows and bag on the ground and sat down.

While he was eating, he heard a noise. He looked up and saw a big bear. The bear was angry and hungry, and it wanted to eat the hunter. The hunter was scared and jumped up. He reached for his bow and arrows, but they were gone. The bear had taken them while he was not looking.

"Help! Help!" the hunter shouted. "The bear has my bow and arrows! I have nothing to fight with!"

But no one heard him. He was alone in the forest. He tried to run away, but the bear was faster. It caught him and ate him. The hunter was gone.

The bear was happy and full. It took the hunter's bag and went to its cave. Inside the bag, it found some more bread and a shiny thing. It was a necklace that the hunter had stolen from a rich lady. The bear did not know what it was, but it liked it. It put it around its neck and felt proud.

The end.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play games, but they are very competitive. They always want to win and be the best.

One day, they play a game of tag in the garden. Tim is it, and he runs after Sam. Sam is fast, but Tim is faster. He almost catches Sam, but Sam runs behind a wall.

"Ha ha, you can't get me!" Sam says from behind the wall.

"Yes, I can!" Tim says. He tries to jump over the wall, but it is too high. He falls and hurts his knee.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tim cries. He holds his knee and tears come out of his eyes.

Sam hears Tim cry and feels sorry. He comes out from behind the wall and sees Tim's knee. It is red and has a little blood.

"I'm sorry, Tim. Are you okay?" Sam says.

Tim looks at Sam and sniffles. "No, it hurts a lot. Why did you hide behind the wall?"

Sam says, "I was just playing. I didn't want you to catch me. I wanted to win."

Tim says, "But it's not fun to win if you hurt someone. You should have warned me that the wall was too high."

Sam nods. He says, "You're right. I should have warned you. I'm sorry, Tim. I don't want to be competitive anymore. I want to be your friend."

Tim smiles. He says, "It's okay, Sam. I'm sorry, too. I don't want to be competitive either. I want to be your friend, too."

Sam hugs Tim and says, "Let's go inside and get a band-aid for your knee. And then we can play another game, but this time, we can play together and have fun."

Tim nods and says, "Okay, Sam. That sounds good. I love you, brother."

Sam says, "I love you, too, brother."

Tom and Sue are husband and wife. They live in a small house with a big garden. They like to grow flowers and vegetables in the garden. They also have a dog named Spot and a cat named Fluffy.

One day, Tom and Sue are working in the garden. Spot and Fluffy are playing nearby. Tom is digging a hole for a new plant. Sue is watering the roses. They are happy and sing a song.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise. They look up and see a big bird. The bird is black and white and has a long beak. It is a magpie. The magpie is flying over the garden. It sees something shiny. It is Sue's ring. Sue's ring is gold and has a red stone. It is a gift from Tom. Sue loves her ring.

The magpie wants the ring. It swoops down and tries to grab it. Sue sees the magpie and screams. She pulls her hand away. The magpie misses the ring but hits Sue's face. Sue feels a sharp pain. She cries out.

"Ow! Ow! Ow! The bird slapped me!" Sue says.

Tom hears Sue and runs to her. He sees the magpie flying away. He sees Sue's face. It is red and swollen. He feels angry and sad.

"Are you okay, Sue? That was a bad bird. It hurt you. I'm sorry." Tom says.

He hugs Sue and kisses her face. He takes her to the house. He gets some ice and a cloth. He puts the ice on Sue's face. He tells her to lie down on the couch. He brings her some water and a cookie. He sits next to her and holds her hand.

"Thank you, Tom. You are very kind. You are a good husband. I'm lucky to have you." Sue says.

She smiles and squeezes his hand. She looks at her ring. It is still on her finger. It sparkles in the sun. She is glad the magpie did not take it. She loves her ring. She loves Tom more.

The end.

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and make mud pies. They found a big patch of dirt and some water. They decided to mix them together.

"Look, I made a big mud pie!" Lily said, holding up her hands. "Do you want some?"

Max nodded and took some mud from Lily. He tried to make a ball, but it was too wet and sticky. He dropped it on the ground.

"Oops!" he said. "It's too runny. How do we make it harder?"

Lily thought for a moment. She saw some leaves and sticks nearby. She had an idea.

"Let's put some leaves and sticks in the mud. Maybe they will make it harder." She said.

They picked up some leaves and sticks and mixed them with the mud. They tried to make balls and pies again, but they still didn't work. The leaves and sticks poked out of the mud and made it messy.

"This is not working!" Max said. He was confused. "Why can't we make good mud pies?"

Lily was confused too. She looked at their hands and clothes. They were covered in mud and bits of leaves and sticks. She felt something tickle her nose. She sneezed.

"Ah-choo!" she said.

Max looked at her and laughed. He sneezed too.

"Ah-choo!" he said.

They looked at each other and giggled. They didn't care about the mud pies anymore. They had fun mixing and sneezing. They were happy.

Lily's mom saw what happened and came to Lily. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. That was a very mean boy. Are you and Anna okay?" Lily nodded, but she still cried. She said, "Anna is hurt. She is troubled. She does not like the park. She wants to go home."

On the way home, Lily whispered to Anna, "Don't worry, Anna. You are my best friend. I love you. You have a good spirit. You are brave and kind. You don't complain. You are the best doll ever." Anna did not say anything. She was a doll. But Lily felt that Anna smiled.

Lila and Tom are curious. They go to the man and ask, "What is tuna?"

The man smiles and says, "Tuna is a fish that lives in the water. It is very yummy and good for you. Do you want to buy some?"

Lila and Tom look at the cans. They are old and rusty. They have dirt and bugs on them. They smell bad. Lila and Tom think the cans are filthy.

They shake their heads and say, "No, thank you. We do not want your tuna. Your tuna is filthy. It is not yummy or good for you. It is yucky and bad for you."

The man frowns and says, "No, no, no. My tuna is not filthy. It is fresh and tasty. You are silly and rude. Go away!"

Lila and Tom run away from the man. They do not like him. They do not like his tuna. They go to the playground and have fun. They are happy and hungry. They eat their sandwiches and apples. They are yummy and good for them. They are not yucky and bad for them. They are not filthy.

Lily was a girl who liked to play with dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Ann. Ann had long hair, a pink dress, and a smile. Lily took care of Ann every day. She brushed her hair, gave her tea, and sang to her.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and Ann. She saw some other kids playing with a big staff. It was a long stick with a star on top. It looked like a magic staff. Lily wanted to play with it too.

"Can I have a turn with your staff?" Lily asked the boy who had it.

"No, it's mine. Go away," the boy said. He was rude and mean.

"Stop it! You are a bad boy! Give me the staff!"

The boy did not listen. He swung the staff at Lily and Ann. He hit Ann on the head. Ann's head cracked and fell off. Lily saw her doll's face on the ground. She felt a big pain in her heart.

She started to cry. She picked up Ann's head and hugged it. She looked at the boy with hate.

"You broke Ann! You broke my best friend! I hate you!"

"I'm so sorry, Lily. That boy was very mean. He should not have done that. We can get you a new doll, okay?"

Lily shook her head. She did not want a new doll. She wanted Ann. She wanted her to be whole again. She wanted to take care of her. She wanted to play with her.

But she could not. Ann was broken. Lily was broken too. She cried and cried. She did not stop.

Tim stops his car. He is nice. He wants to help Jen. He says, "OK, Jen. I will wait for you. Reverse your car and fix it."

Jen smiles. She reverses her car. But she does not fix it. She pushes it back to the start. She says, "Now I am ready. Let's race again."

Tim is confused. He says, "But Jen, you cheated. You did not fix your car. You just went back to the start. That is not fair."

Jen says, "No, I did not cheat. I reversed my car. That is a rule. You can reverse your car too."

Lily liked to watch the birds in the sky. She saw many kinds of birds, but her favorite was the dove. The dove was white and soft and made a gentle sound. Lily wanted to touch the dove and be its friend.

One day, Lily saw a dove sitting on a branch near her window. She ran to get some bread and opened the window. She threw some bread crumbs to the dove and said, "Hello, dove. I like you. Do you want to be my friend?"

The dove looked at Lily and tilted its head. It flew closer to the window and pecked at the bread. It cooed softly and nodded. Lily smiled and reached out her hand. The dove hopped on her finger and let her stroke its feathers.

Lily was very happy. She said, "You are so nice, dove. I believe you are a magic dove. Can you grant me a wish?"

The dove blinked and nodded again. It whispered in Lily's ear, "I can grant you one wish, but you have to be careful what you wish for. Some wishes are not good for you."

Lily thought for a moment. She said, "I wish I could fly like you, dove. I want to see the world and be free."

The dove sighed and said, "Are you sure, Lily? Flying is not easy. There are many dangers and troubles in the sky. You might miss your home and your family. You might get lost or hurt."

Lily nodded. She said, "I am sure, dove. I want to fly. Please, grant me my wish."

The dove said, "Very well, Lily. I will grant you your wish. But remember, you can only fly for one day. When the sun sets, you will turn back into a girl. And you have to come back to this window, or you will be stuck as a bird forever."

Lily agreed. She said, "Thank you, dove. I will come back, I promise."

The dove touched Lily's nose with its beak and said, "Close your eyes, Lily. And make your wish."

Lily closed her eyes and wished with all her heart. She felt a strange sensation in her body. She felt her arms become wings, her legs become claws, her hair become feathers. She opened her eyes and saw that she had turned into a dove. A pale dove, like the one on her finger.

She gasped and said, "Wow, dove. You did it. You made me a dove."

The dove smiled and said, "Yes, Lily. I did. Now, let's fly. But don't forget your promise."

Lily nodded and said, "I won't, dove. Let's fly."

They flew out of the window and into the sky. They soared and glided and circled and dived. They saw many things and had many adventures. Lily was happy and free. She felt like she was living a dream.

But she did not know that the dove had a secret. A secret that would change everything. A secret that would make her wish come true in a way she did not expect. A secret that would make her regret her wish. A secret that would make her cry. A secret that would make her pale.

One day, Sara found a new doll in her box. It was very pretty, with long hair and a shiny dress. She showed it to Tom and said, "Look, Tom, I have a new doll. She is so nice. Do you want to play with her?"

But you did not take care of it and you ruined it. Now you have no doll and no car. You have to learn to respect your toys and your siblings."

She took the broken doll and the box of cars and put them away. She said, "You can have your toys back when you show me that you can play nicely and share. Now go to your rooms and think about what you did."

"Let's make them go high in the sky!" Tom said.

"But how?" Lily asked.

"Be careful, Tom!" Lily said. "That could be dangerous!"

But Tom did not listen. He threw the match into the box and waited for the fireworks to happen. But nothing happened. He went closer to the box and looked inside.

Suddenly, there was a loud bang and a bright flash. The fireworks exploded in Tom's face. He screamed and fell to the ground. Lily ran to him and saw that he was hurt. His eyes were red and his skin was burned. She cried and called for help.

Soon, their parents and a doctor came. They took Tom to the hospital and treated his wounds. Lily stayed with him and hugged him. She was sorry for what happened.

"I'm sorry, Tom," she said. "I should have stopped you."

"I'm sorry, too, Lily," Tom said. "I should have listened to you. I was foolish and reckless. I learned my lesson. Fireworks are not toys. They are dangerous and can hurt us. We should never play with them."

Lily nodded and kissed his cheek. They both learned a valuable lesson that day. They promised to be more careful and respectful of fireworks. They also thanked their parents and the doctor for helping them. They hoped that Tom would heal soon and that they could play outside again. But they would never touch fireworks again.

One day, they went to the park with their mom and brought their big red boat. They saw a small stream that flowed under a bridge. They thought it would be fun to sail their boat there. They put their boat in the water and watched it go under the bridge and come out on the other side.

"Wow, our boat is so fast and strong!" Lila said.

"Yes, it is the best boat ever!" Ben agreed.

They saw another boy who was also playing with a toy boat. His boat was smaller and green, and it looked old and worn. He was trying to sail it in the stream, but it kept getting stuck on the rocks and the weeds.

"Look at that silly boat!" Lila laughed. "It is so slow and weak!"

"Yeah, it is the worst boat ever!" Ben echoed.

They ran to the bridge and shouted at the boy.

"Hey, your boat is no good! You should get a new one like ours!"

The boy looked sad and said, "I can't. This is the only boat I have. My grandpa gave it to me before he died. He said it was his favorite toy when he was a kid. He said it was a humble boat, but it had a big heart."

Lila and Ben felt ashamed. They realized they had been mean and rude to the boy. They remembered that their mom had taught them to be kind and respectful to others, and to be grateful for what they had.

They ran to the boy and said, "We are sorry. We didn't mean to hurt your feelings. Your boat is very special and beautiful. Can we play with you?"

The boy smiled and said, "Sure. Thank you. You are very nice. Can I see your boat?"

They showed him their big red boat and let him hold it. They told him how their dad had made it for them. They said it was a fast and strong boat, but it also had a big heart.

They played together for a long time, sailing their boats in the stream and making friends. They learned that it didn't matter how big or small, how new or old, how fast or slow their boats were. What mattered was how they treated each other and how they enjoyed their toys.

They also learned that broccoli was good for them and ate it for dinner without complaining. The end.

He sees another worm nearby. It is pale and still. It does not move. Ben thinks it is sick or asleep. He grabs it easily and holds it in his hand. He feels happy and proud. He runs to his mom and shows her the worm.

But his mom does not look happy. She looks scared and grossed out. She tells Ben to drop the worm and wash his hands. She says it is not a worm, but a snake. A pale snake that can bite and hurt. Mia and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and zebras. Mia liked the pandas best. They were black and white and fluffy. They ate bamboo and rolled on the grass.

"Look, Ben, that panda is whistling!" Mia said, pointing to a panda that made a funny sound with its mouth.

"No, it's not. Pandas can't whistle. You're silly, Mia." Ben said, laughing.

"Yes, it is. I heard it. You're mean, Ben." Mia said, frowning.

They started to argue. Mom and Dad heard them and came over.

"What's wrong, kids?" Mom asked.

"Mia says that panda is whistling, but it's not. She's lying." Ben said.

"No, I'm not. I heard it. Ben is teasing me." Mia said.

Mom and Dad looked at the panda. It made the sound again.

"That's not whistling, Mia. That's how pandas communicate. They make different sounds to talk to each other." Dad explained.

"Really? What is it saying?" Mia asked, curious.

"Well, I don't know for sure, but maybe it's saying it's hungry, or it wants to play, or it's happy." Dad said.

"Wow, that's cool. I wish I could talk to pandas." Mia said.

"Me too. I'm sorry I laughed at you, Mia. You're not silly, you're smart." Ben said.

"It's okay, Ben. I'm sorry I called you mean. You're not mean, you're nice." Mia said.

They hugged and smiled. Mom and Dad were happy to see them get along.

"Come on, kids. Let's go see the other animals. Maybe we can hear them talk too." Mom said.

They followed Mom and Dad to the next exhibit. They had a fun day at the zoo. They learned a lot about animals and how they live. They also learned to listen to each other and be kind.

Tim and Lily turn around. They see their papers. They are blank. They see their crayons. They are gone. They see their eraser. It is smiling.

Tim and Lily are sad. They cry. They want their drawings back. They want their crayons back. They want their animals and flowers and cars back. They want their songs back.

She saw a small sunflower on the ground. It was not tall and pretty. It was brown and wilted and disgusting. She did not like it. But she thought, maybe her mom would like it anyway. She picked it up and ran to her mom.

She gave the sunflower to her mom and said, "I got this for you, mom. I love you." Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Thank you, Lily. I love you too. And I love this sunflower. It is very special."

Lily was confused. She said, "But mom, it is disgusting. It is not big and yellow and happy. It is brown and wilted and sad." Her mom said, "No, Lily. It is not disgusting. It is beautiful. Because you gave it to me with love. And love makes everything beautiful."

Lily learned a lesson. She learned that it is not how things look that matters. It is how you feel about them. And she learned that love is the best gift of all.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to help their mom cook. One day, mom asked them to make some soup for dad, who was sick. Lily and Ben put some water, carrots, potatoes and chicken in a big pot. They stirred and stirred with a big spoon.

"Soup is good for dad," Lily said. "It will make him warm and happy."

"Yes, and we can give him a scarf too," Ben said. "A scarf will keep his neck cozy."

They looked for a scarf in the closet, but they could not find one. They saw a ball of wool and some needles. They had an idea.

"Let's make a scarf for dad," Lily said. "We can knit it with the wool and the needles."

They tried to knit, but it was hard. They made many knots and holes. The wool was scratchy and the needles were pointy. They got frustrated and sad.

"Knitting is not fun," Ben said. "It hurts my fingers and makes me angry."

"Me too," Lily said. "And our scarf is ugly and small. Dad will not like it."

They heard mom call them from the kitchen. "Lily and Ben, the soup is ready. Come and taste it."

They left the wool and the needles on the floor and ran to the kitchen. They tasted the soup and it was delicious. They smiled and hugged mom.

"Mom, you are the best cook," Lily said. "Your soup is yummy and smooth."

"Thank you, my loves," mom said. "You are very good helpers. I'm sure dad will love the soup too. And look, I have a surprise for you."

She showed them a big, soft, colorful scarf that she had knitted for dad. It had stripes of red, blue, green and yellow. It was long and warm.

"Wow, mom, you are the best knitter too," Ben said. "Your scarf is beautiful and big."

"Thank you, my loves," mom said. "I knitted it while you were making the soup. I used the wool and the needles that you left on the floor. I'm sorry, I hope you don't mind."

Lily and Ben looked at each other and felt ashamed. They had wasted the wool and the needles and made a mess. They had not finished their scarf and had given up.

"Mom, we are sorry," Lily said. "We wanted to make a scarf for dad too, but we could not do it. We did not know how to knit. We made a bad scarf and a big mess."

"Mom, we are sorry," Ben said. "We should have asked you to teach us how to knit. We should have tried harder and been more patient. We did not do our best."

Mom hugged them and kissed them. "It's okay, my loves," she said. "I'm proud of you for wanting to make a scarf for dad. That was very kind and thoughtful of you. But knitting is not easy. It takes time and practice and skill. You can't learn it in one day. You have to be willing to make mistakes and learn from them. You have to keep trying and not give up. That's how you get better at anything."

Lily and Ben nodded and understood. They felt sorry for their bad scarf and their big mess, but they also felt happy for their good soup and their mom's scarf. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that cooking and knitting are both ways of showing love, but they also require effort and perseverance. They learned that they can do anything if they try hard and ask for help.

They gave mom a big hug and said, "We love you, mom. Thank you for teaching us how to cook and knit. We want to learn more from you. We want to do our best."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, my loves. You are my best gifts. Come on, let's go and give dad the soup and the scarf. He will be very happy to see you."

Lily was a little bunny who loved to hop. She hopped all over the meadow, looking for something to eat. She was very hungry, but she could not find any carrots or lettuce.

She saw a big oak tree in the corner of the meadow. She hopped towards it, hoping to find some acorns. But when she got there, she saw a big owl sitting on a branch. The owl looked at her with his big eyes and said, "Who are you?"

Lily was scared of the owl. She knew that owls liked to eat bunnies. She said, "I am Lily, a little bunny. I am looking for some food. Please do not eat me!"

The owl said, "I am not hungry, little bunny. I ate a mouse for breakfast. But you should not come near my tree. This is my home, and I do not like visitors."

Lily said, "I am sorry, Mr. Owl. I did not know this was your home. I will go away and find another place to eat."

The owl said, "That is a good idea, little bunny. But be careful, there are other animals in the meadow who might want to eat you. You should hop fast and stay with your friends."

Lily said, "Thank you, Mr. Owl. You are very wise and kind. Goodbye!" She hopped away from the oak tree, looking for a safer spot to find some food. She hoped to find some carrots or lettuce soon. She was still very hungry.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play at the beach. They built sand castles, dug holes, and collected shells. But their favorite thing was to splash in the water. They ran into the waves and kicked their feet, laughing and shouting.

One day, the tide was very high and the water was very fast. Tom and Sam did not notice, because they were having too much fun. They splashed and splashed, until they were far from the shore. Then they heard their mom calling them.

"Tom! Sam! Come back! The tide is too strong!" she yelled.

Tom and Sam tried to swim back, but the water pushed them away. They were scared and troubled. They did not know what to do.

"Help! Help!" they cried.

Their mom saw a lifeguard nearby and waved at him. The lifeguard saw the boys and quickly swam to them. He grabbed them by their arms and pulled them to his boat. He took them back to the shore, where their mom hugged them and thanked him.

"Are you okay, boys?" she asked.

"Yes, mom, we are okay," they said.

"I'm glad you are safe, but you have to be careful. The tide can be dangerous. You have to stay close to me and listen to me when I call you. Do you understand?" she said.

"Yes, mom, we understand. We are sorry. We won't splash too far again," they said.

They learned their lesson and never went too far into the water again. They still liked to splash, but they always watched the tide and listened to their mom.

Lily was very sad. She did not want to punish Spot. She did not want to lose her friend. She cried and begged mom to let her keep the frog.

The frog croaked sadly and swam away. Lily watched it go and cried. She wished she could play with Spot again. She wished mom would understand. She wished frogs and people could be friends.

Ben stopped crying and smiled. He said he was OK. He said he liked ducks too and wanted to be friends with them. He said he was grateful for his mom and Lily.

Mom smiled and hugged them both. She said she was proud of them for being brave and kind. She said she loved them very much.

They all watched the duck for a while. Then they decided to play somewhere else. They left the puddle and the duck in peace. They had a fun day in the park.

Lily was very happy. She had an invitation to Ben's birthday party. She liked Ben. He was her friend. He had a big house with a swing and a slide. She wanted to play with him and eat cake.

She put on her pink dress and her shiny shoes. She took her gift for Ben. It was a book with animals. She loved animals. She hoped Ben would love them too.

She walked with her mom to Ben's house. She saw many cars and balloons. She heard music and laughter. She ran to the door and rang the bell.

Ben's mom opened the door. She smiled at Lily and her mom. She said, "Hello, Lily. Come in. Ben is waiting for you. He is very excited to see you."

Lily followed Ben's mom to the living room. She saw many kids and toys. She looked for Ben. She saw him in a corner. He was holding a big teddy bear. He looked sad.

Lily went to him and said, "Hi, Ben. Happy birthday. I brought you a gift. It is a book with animals. Do you want to see it?"

Ben looked at Lily and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very nice. But I don't want to see it. I don't want to play. I don't want to have a party. I want to be alone."

Lily was confused. She asked, "Why, Ben? Why are you sad? Why don't you want to have fun?"

Ben hugged his teddy bear and said, "Because my dog is dead. He was my best friend. He was old and sick. He died yesterday. I miss him so much. I don't care about anything else."

Lily felt sorry for Ben. She knew how it felt to lose someone. She had lost her grandma last year. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I know how you feel. I lost my grandma. She was my best friend too. She was old and sick. She died too. I miss her so much too."

Ben looked at Lily and said, "You do? You understand me?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I understand you. And I want to be your friend. Can I hug you?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, you can. Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. Can I see your book?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, you can. Come, let's see it together. Maybe we can find your dog and my grandma in it. Maybe they are happy in heaven."

Ben smiled and said, "Maybe they are. Come, let's go."

They held hands and walked to the couch. They opened the book and looked at the animals. They found a dog and a grandma. They pointed at them and said, "There they are. There they are."

They hugged each other and laughed. They felt a little better. They had each other. They had a new friend.

Lila and Tom liked to play in the garden. They had many flowers and plants. They watered them every day. They liked the sunflowers best. They were big and yellow and happy.

One day, they saw a new sunflower. It was very small and green. They wanted to help it grow. They gave it more water and more sun. They talked to it and sang to it.

"Hello, little sunflower," Lila said. "You are so cute. We are your friends. We will make you healthy and strong."

"Yes, little sunflower," Tom said. "You are so lucky. You have a good home. We will make you happy and bright."

But the little sunflower did not grow. It did not turn yellow. It did not smile. It started to turn brown and black. It started to smell bad. It started to rot.

Lila and Tom were sad and scared. They did not know what to do. They asked their mom for help.

"Mom, mom, look at our sunflower," Lila said. "It is sick. It is dying. Can you fix it?"

"Mom, mom, please help our sunflower," Tom said. "It is not happy. It is not bright. Can you save it?"

Mom looked at the sunflower. She shook her head. She said, "I'm sorry, Lila and Tom. This sunflower is not a sunflower. It is a weed. It is not good for the garden. It is not good for the other flowers. It has to go."

She pulled out the weed and threw it in the trash. Lila and Tom cried. They felt bad. They had lost their sunflower. They had lost their friend. They had made a mistake.

Lily and her mom went to the grocery store. Lily liked to look at all the things on the shelves. She saw some fruits, some bread, some milk, and some cookies. She wanted to buy some cookies, but her mom said no.

"Mom, please, can I have some cookies?" Lily asked.

"No, Lily, you already had some at home. We need to buy healthy food, not junk food." Her mom said.

Lily was sad. She did not like healthy food. She liked sweet and crunchy food. She saw a display of cookies near the cash register. The display had a sign that said "Buy one, get one free". The cookies looked very yummy. They had chocolate chips and nuts and raisins. Lily wanted to try them.

She sneaked away from her mom and grabbed a bag of cookies from the display. She opened it and took a big bite. The cookie was thick and chewy. It tasted very good. Lily smiled.

But then, her mom saw her. Her mom was angry. She took the bag of cookies from Lily and put it back on the display. She scolded Lily for being naughty and greedy.

"Lily, how could you do that? You know you are not supposed to take things without paying. And you know you are not supposed to eat cookies before dinner. You are in big trouble, young lady." Her mom said.

Lily felt bad. She knew she did something wrong. She said sorry to her mom and to the store lady. She promised to be good and to eat healthy food. She hoped her mom would forgive her and still love her.

Tom was a fat cat who liked to sleep in a sack. He had a sack in every room of the house, and he would curl up in them and snore. He did not like to play or run or chase mice. He only liked to eat and sleep.

One day, a new cat came to the house. Her name was Lily, and she was thin and fast and playful. She saw Tom sleeping in his sack in the living room, and she wanted to play with him. She jumped on the sack and pounced on Tom.

"Hey, wake up, fat cat!" she said. "Let's play!"

Tom did not like that. He hissed and scratched at Lily, and tried to hide in his sack. But Lily did not stop. She kept jumping and pouncing and biting at Tom, until he ran away to another room.

Tom was scared and angry. He did not want to play with Lily. He wanted to sleep in his sack. He ran to the bedroom, where he had another sack on the bed. He hoped Lily would not find him there.

But Lily followed him. She saw him hiding in his sack on the bed, and she jumped on the bed too. She said, "Come on, fat cat, don't be a scaredy-cat! Playing is fun!"

Tom did not think playing was fun. He thought playing was mean and hurtful. He cried and whimpered in his sack, and wished Lily would leave him alone.

Then, he heard a voice. It was his human, who came to the bedroom. He saw Tom and Lily on the bed, and he knew what was happening. He picked up Lily and said, "No, no, Lily, you can't play like that. You are hurting Tom. He is a good cat, and he likes to sleep in his sack. You have to be nice to him."

He put Lily down on the floor, and gave her a ball to play with. He said, "Here, Lily, this is your toy. You can play with this, and leave Tom alone. He is not your toy. He is your friend."

He then went to Tom, and stroked his fur. He said, "It's okay, Tom, you are safe. I'm sorry Lily was mean to you. She is a new cat, and she does not know better. She will learn to be nice, and you will learn to like her. You are both my cats, and I love you both."

He lifted Tom out of his sack, and hugged him. He said, "You are a fat cat, but you are a sweet cat. You don't have to play if you don't want to. You can sleep in your sack, and I will comfort you."

Tom felt better. He purred and licked his human's face. He was glad his human was there to comfort him. He looked at Lily, who was playing with her ball. He thought maybe she was not so bad, after all. Maybe he could play with her, sometimes. But not now. Now, he wanted to sleep in his sack. He crawled back into his sack, and closed his eyes. He was a happy cat.

Tim and Anna are twins. They like to play in the kitchen with Mom. Mom is making salad for lunch. She has many things on the table: lettuce, tomato, cheese, and avocado.

"Mom, what is that green thing?" Tim asks, pointing at the avocado.

"That is an avocado, Tim. It is a fruit. It is good for you. Do you want to try some?" Mom says.

"Yes, please!" Tim says. He likes to try new things.

Mom cuts the avocado in half and gives Tim a spoon. He scoops out some of the soft green flesh and puts it in his mouth. He makes a funny face.

"Yuck! I don't like it. It is mushy and bitter!" Tim says, spitting it out.

Anna laughs. She thinks Tim is silly. She wants to try the avocado too.

"Can I have some, Mom?" Anna asks.

"Sure, Anna. Here you go." Mom says, giving Anna the other half of the avocado and a spoon.

Anna scoops out some of the avocado and puts it in her mouth. She smiles.

"Yum! I like it. It is creamy and sweet!" Anna says, swallowing it.

Tim looks at Anna. He does not understand how she can like the avocado.

"Anna, you are mighty. You can eat anything!" Tim says.

Anna giggles. She likes to be mighty.

"Thank you, Tim. You are mighty too. You can try anything!" Anna says.

Mom smiles. She is proud of her twins. She gives them both a hug and a kiss.

"Good job, Tim and Anna. You are both mighty and brave. Now, let's finish the salad and eat lunch!" Mom says.
